# Build Plan — "Heard"

Phased milestones for Claude Code. Work **in order**; each milestone ends with green types, lint, tests, and (for any screen) an axe pass. Check items off as you go. See `SPEC.md` for detail and `CLAUDE.md` for the rules.

Legend: every milestone has **Tasks** and **Done when** (acceptance criteria).

---

## M0 — Foundation & auth
**Tasks**
- [ ] Scaffold Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript (`strict`) + Tailwind; ESLint + Prettier; Vitest + RTL + Playwright; CI (typecheck + lint + test).
- [ ] Create Supabase project; wire `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts`; add `.env.example` (see `SPEC.md` §9).
- [ ] Set up i18n message catalog `messages/en.json`; no hard-coded UI strings thereafter.
- [ ] Build `components/ui` primitives (Button, Field/Input, Select, Card, Dialog, Toast, Tag/Chip, Avatar, FocusRing) using the warm/trustworthy tokens from the design brief. Accessible by construction.
- [ ] Email+password auth (Supabase): `/signin`, `/signup` with **role selection** (customer or provider); create `profiles` row on sign-up; provider sign-up also creates a `providers` row (`status=pending`).
- [ ] App shell: header/nav, the persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" affordance, route groups for customer/provider/admin.

**Done when:** a user can sign up/in as customer or provider, role is persisted, every primitive passes axe, CI is green.

---

## M1 — Data model, RLS, seed
**Tasks**
- [ ] Write SQL migrations for all tables in `SPEC.md` §4 (profiles, providers, availability_slots, bookings, sessions, payments, payouts, reviews, reports).
- [ ] Add **RLS policies** per table (owner-scoped; public reads approved-provider public fields; admin all).
- [ ] `supabase/seed.sql`: 6 sample providers (varied names, topics, languages, ratings, prices, availability) + 1 admin + 1 customer.
- [ ] `lib/db/queries.ts` and `lib/validation/schemas.ts` (Zod) for all entities.

**Done when:** `supabase db reset` applies cleanly with seed data; RLS verified (a customer cannot read another customer's bookings).

---

## M2 — Integration adapters (mock)
**Tasks**
- [ ] `payments/interface.ts` + `mock.ts` (in-DB ledger; synthetic refs) + `real.ts` (stubbed `// TODO: Stripe Connect`) + `index.ts` (selects by `INTEGRATIONS_MODE`).
- [ ] `calls/interface.ts` + `mock.ts` (synthetic refs; UI renders mock call) + `real.ts` (`// TODO: Zoom Meeting SDK`) + `index.ts`.
- [ ] `background-check/interface.ts` + `mock.ts` (`pending`) + `real.ts` (`// TODO: Checkr`) + `index.ts`.
- [ ] `lib/pricing.ts`: `priceForBlock`, overage, commission (from config), tips, half-up rounding — all pure.

**Done when:** unit tests cover every mock adapter and all `pricing` cases; feature code can call `getPayments()/getCalls()/getBackgroundCheck()`; no direct mock/real imports elsewhere.

---

## M3 — Provider side
**Tasks**
- [ ] `/provider/onboarding`: step-based, audio-first — record/upload **voice intro** to Storage, pick topics + languages, set block prices + overage rate, set availability; on finish call `backgroundCheck.initiate()` → `bg_check_status=pending`.
- [ ] `/provider/dashboard`: large **"Available now"** toggle (labeled text state), upcoming sessions, weekly earnings, rating.
- [ ] Accessibility: verify the whole onboarding flow by keyboard + screen-reader semantics (this is the showcase flow).

**Done when:** a seeded provider can complete onboarding, lands in `pending`, and the dashboard reflects availability/earnings; axe passes on both screens.

---

## M4 — Admin: provider approval
**Tasks**
- [ ] `/admin/providers`: queue of `pending` providers with details + voice-intro playback; **Approve / Reject / Suspend** actions (set `providers.status` and `bg_check_status`).
- [ ] Guard admin routes/actions by role.

**Done when:** an admin approves a provider and that provider becomes eligible to appear in browse; non-admins are blocked (RLS + route guard).

---

## M5 — Customer discovery & booking
**Tasks**
- [ ] `/` welcome; `/browse` with filters (topic, language, available-now, price) and **voice-intro players**; `/listeners/[id]` profile (voice intro, bio, topics, reviews, "Talk now"/"Schedule").
- [ ] `/book/[providerId]`: choose block (15/30/45) + now/scheduled; price summary; mock payment → `payments.authorizeHold(price_block)`; create `booking` (`confirmed`).

**Done when:** a customer can find an approved provider by voice and complete a booking with an authorized hold recorded in `payments`; lists reflect only `approved` providers.

---

## M6 — Session lifecycle
**Tasks**
- [ ] `/session/[id]` pre-call (waiting room) → in-call **mock screen**: avatar + waveform, **count-up timer**, mute, captions toggle, end. Provider side mirrors it under `/provider/session/[id]` (incoming → accept → in-session, with a "Report / End for safety" control).
- [ ] On end: compute elapsed → `pricing` (block + overage + 5% commission + provider earnings) → `payments.capture(total)` → write `session` (`completed`).

**Done when:** a full mock call runs, the timer drives elapsed time, and final accounting is correct and persisted (verified by unit tests on the pricing path).

---

## M7 — Reviews, tips, payouts
**Tasks**
- [ ] `/session/[id]/summary`: rating (1–5) + optional **tip** (Skip equally prominent) + receipt; write `review`, recompute provider rating, add tip to earnings (no commission on tips).
- [ ] Weekly payout job (mock): `payments.runWeeklyPayouts()` aggregates earnings into `payouts`; show payout history on the provider dashboard.

**Done when:** rating/tip update the provider correctly and a mock weekly payout row is generated and visible.

---

## M8 — Accessibility & visual polish
**Tasks**
- [ ] Full pass against `SPEC.md` §10 + the design brief: focus order, live-region announcements (availability, "call connected", booking confirmed), 200% zoom, reduced-motion, contrast.
- [ ] Apply the warm/trustworthy styling consistently; calm, uncluttered, no dark patterns.
- [ ] Confirm the "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" affordance on every page + a minimal "Report a problem" hook that writes to `reports`.

**Done when:** every screen passes axe; manual keyboard-only walkthrough of both happy paths succeeds.

---

## M9 — Tests, docs, handoff
**Tasks**
- [ ] Unit: pricing, adapters, schemas. Component: core screens + axe. **E2E (Playwright):** (a) customer browse→book→mock session→rate; (b) provider onboard→admin approve→appears in browse.
- [ ] `README.md`: setup, env, `supabase` migrate/seed, running tests, and **how to swap a mock adapter for a real one** (Stripe/Zoom/Checkr) when accounts are ready.
- [ ] Confirm `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles and reaches the `// TODO` stubs without breaking the build.

**Done when:** CI green; both E2E paths pass; README lets a newcomer run the app in `mock` mode in minutes.

---

### After this build (fast-follows, not now)
Wire real **Stripe Connect** (Express host of funds + payouts), real **Zoom Meeting SDK** (platform-owned host pool + S2S OAuth + webhook metering — see the Zoom Meeting SDK guide), real **Checkr**; add the **moderation/reporting admin UI**; native mobile; tips/subscription as a second revenue line (relevant given the 5% commission).

# CLAUDE.md — "Heard"

Conventions and guardrails for building this app. **Read `SPEC.md` for the full spec and `BUILD_PLAN.md` for the milestone order.** This file holds the rules you must follow on every change.

## What this is
A two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind or visually impaired. Non-clinical companionship — **never** therapy. Accessibility and the dignity of providers are the whole point of the product.

## Stack
Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage) · Tailwind CSS · Zod · Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright · deploy to Vercel + Supabase.

## Golden rules (do not violate)
1. **Accessibility is non-negotiable.** WCAG 2.2 AA minimum, AAA contrast on body text. Keyboard-operable, visible focus, semantic HTML, labeled controls, no state by color alone. A screen isn't done until it passes axe in tests. See `SPEC.md` §10.
2. **External services only through adapters.** Reach payments/calls/background-checks via `lib/integrations/*/index.ts` (`getPayments()`, `getCalls()`, `getBackgroundCheck()`). Never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly; never call Stripe/Zoom/Checkr SDKs outside `real.ts`. Default mode is `mock`.
3. **All money is integer cents.** No floats for currency. All pricing/commission math lives in `lib/pricing.ts` and nowhere else. Commission comes from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE` (config), never a literal.
4. **Security: RLS on every table.** Customers/providers touch only their own rows; public reads only approved-provider public fields; admin sees all. The `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is server-only — never shipped to the client, never in a client component.
5. **Validate at the boundary.** Every server action and route handler validates input with Zod and checks the caller's role/ownership before doing work.
6. **Server-first.** Prefer React Server Components + Server Actions; use client components only for genuinely interactive UI. No secrets in client bundles.
7. **All user-facing copy goes through `messages/en.json`** (i18n-ready) — no hard-coded strings in components.
8. **Safety framing in the product.** Every page carries the "companionship, not therapy — crisis support" affordance. Don't add anything that implies medical/mental-health treatment.

## Conventions
- Components: PascalCase files; one component per file; design-system primitives in `components/ui` (Button, Field, Card, Dialog, …) used everywhere for consistent a11y.
- Styling: Tailwind core utilities + the design tokens from `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` (warm & trustworthy palette, 18px+ body, ≥48px tap targets).
- Data access: queries in `lib/db/queries.ts`; Zod schemas in `lib/validation/schemas.ts`.
- Errors: never swallow; return typed results and show friendly, accessible error states.
- Tests live in `tests/`; add/extend tests with every feature.

## Commands
```
npm run dev            # local dev
npm run build          # production build
npm run lint           # eslint + prettier
npm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
npm run test           # vitest (unit + component)
npm run test:e2e       # playwright
supabase db reset      # apply migrations + seed (6 sample providers)
```

## Definition of done (every feature/PR)
- TypeScript passes (`strict`), lint clean.
- Keyboard-navigable + axe a11y check passes for any new/changed screen.
- New logic has unit tests; pricing/accounting changes have explicit cases (blocks, overage, commission, tips, rounding).
- Inputs Zod-validated; RLS/ownership respected; no secrets client-side.
- User-facing strings in `messages/en.json`.

## Out of scope right now
Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr calls, moderation/reporting admin UI (table + minimal report hook only), native mobile, subscriptions. Keep schema/adapters ready so these don't need a rewrite. See `SPEC.md` §12.

# Build Specification — "Heard" (working name)

> A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with, and be listened to by, professional **companion listeners — all of whom are legally blind or visually impaired.** Non-clinical companionship and conversation. US market, English (i18n-ready).

**This document is the full build spec for Claude Code.** Read it together with `CLAUDE.md` (conventions Claude Code must follow) and `BUILD_PLAN.md` (the phased milestone plan). The UI/UX is specified separately in `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` — follow it for screens, components, palette, and accessibility detail.

---

## 1. Decisions locked for this build

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Build approach | **App-first.** Build the whole app end-to-end now; Stripe, Zoom, and Checkr are **mocked behind adapters** and swapped for real later. |
| Stack | **Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Supabase + Tailwind CSS.** Deploy target Vercel + Supabase. |
| Pricing | **Hybrid:** fixed blocks of **15 / 30 / 45 min** at a set price, plus **per-minute overage** if the call runs past the block. |
| Commission | **5%** platform fee (provider keeps 95%). Stored as config (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`), never hard-coded. |
| Payouts | Weekly (mocked). |
| Auth | **Email + password** (Supabase Auth). Roles: `customer`, `provider`, `admin`. |
| Languages | **English only**, but i18n-ready (all copy via message catalog). |
| Admin scope | **Provider approval only** (approve/reject/suspend). Reporting & moderation UI are **deferred** (see §12). |
| Accessibility | **WCAG 2.2 AA minimum**, AAA contrast on body text. Non-negotiable. |

> **Honest note carried into the build:** at 5% commission, per-session margin is thin after payment fees. `lib/pricing.ts` centralizes the rate so it is trivial to change, and the schema supports tips and (future) subscriptions as additional revenue.

---

## 2. Product overview

Customers arrive lonely or wanting company. They discover a listener by hearing a short **voice intro**, book a **session block**, and have an audio conversation. Providers are blind/visually-impaired adults working from home by screen reader; the product exists to give them dignified, flexible income. The whole experience must be calm, warm, trustworthy, and operable entirely by keyboard and screen reader.

**Core promise to reflect everywhere:** companionship, *not therapy*. A persistent, gentle "companionship, not medical or mental-health care — if you're in crisis, find support" affordance appears on every screen.

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 High level
- **Next.js App Router** app on Vercel. React Server Components + Server Actions for data work; client components only for interactive UI.
- **Supabase** for Postgres, Auth (email+password), and Storage (voice intros, avatars). **Row-Level Security on every table.**
- **Route handlers** (`app/api/**`) for webhooks (used by the *real* adapters later) and any server endpoints.
- **Zod** validates every input at the boundary (server actions, route handlers).
- All external services (**payments, calls, background checks**) are reached **only** through adapter interfaces — never called directly from feature code.

### 3.2 The adapter pattern (the most important rule)

Each external concern has: an **interface**, a **mock implementation** (default, used in this build), a **real implementation** (stubbed with `// TODO: real integration` for later), and an **`index.ts`** that selects one based on `INTEGRATIONS_MODE` (`mock` | `real`).

```
lib/integrations/
  payments/        interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
  calls/           interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
  background-check/ interface.ts  mock.ts  real.ts  index.ts
```

**PaymentsProvider** (maps to Stripe Connect later)
```ts
interface PaymentsProvider {
  ensureCustomer(userId: string): Promise<{ customerRef: string }>;
  authorizeHold(p: { bookingId: string; amountCents: number; customerRef: string }): Promise<{ paymentRef: string; status: "authorized" }>;
  capture(p: { paymentRef: string; amountCents: number }): Promise<{ status: "captured" }>;
  refund(p: { paymentRef: string; amountCents: number }): Promise<{ status: "refunded" }>;
  ensureConnectedAccount(providerId: string): Promise<{ accountRef: string }>;
  recordProviderEarning(p: { providerId: string; amountCents: number; sessionId: string }): Promise<void>;
  runWeeklyPayouts(): Promise<{ payouts: Array<{ providerId: string; amountCents: number }> }>;
}
```
*Mock:* writes an in-DB ledger (`payments`, `payouts`) and returns synthetic refs (`mock_pay_…`). No money moves.

**CallProvider** (maps to Zoom Meeting SDK later)
```ts
interface CallProvider {
  createSession(p: { bookingId: string; providerId: string; customerId: string; maxMinutes: number }): Promise<{ callSessionRef: string }>;
  getJoinInfo(p: { callSessionRef: string; role: "host" | "participant"; userId: string }): Promise<{ joinRef: string; mockMode: boolean }>;
  endSession(p: { callSessionRef: string }): Promise<{ endedAt: string }>;
}
```
*Mock:* returns synthetic refs; the UI renders the **in-app mock call screen** (avatar + waveform, count-up timer, mute, captions, end). No real audio. The timer is the source of truth for elapsed time in mock mode.

**BackgroundCheckProvider** (maps to Checkr later)
```ts
interface BackgroundCheckProvider {
  initiate(p: { providerId: string }): Promise<{ checkRef: string; status: "pending" }>;
  getStatus(p: { checkRef: string }): Promise<{ status: "pending" | "clear" | "consider" }>;
}
```
*Mock:* returns `pending`; an **admin** clears the provider manually (stands in for Checkr).

> **Rule:** feature code imports `getPayments()`, `getCalls()`, `getBackgroundCheck()` from the integration `index.ts`. It must never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and never reference Stripe/Zoom/Checkr SDKs outside `real.ts`.

---

## 4. Data model (Postgres / Supabase)

Money is always **integer cents**. Timestamps are `timestamptz`. All tables have `id uuid default gen_random_uuid()`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. Define as SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/` with **RLS policies** and a `supabase/seed.sql`.

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `profiles` | `id` (FK `auth.users`), `role` (`customer`/`provider`/`admin`), `full_name`, `email`, `locale` | One row per user, created on sign-up. |
| `providers` | `id` (FK `profiles`), `display_name`, `bio`, `voice_intro_path`, `avatar_color`, `status` (`pending`/`approved`/`rejected`/`suspended`), `languages text[]`, `topics text[]`, `price_block_15_cents`, `price_block_30_cents`, `price_block_45_cents`, `overage_per_min_cents`, `is_available_now bool`, `rating_avg numeric`, `rating_count int`, `bg_check_ref`, `bg_check_status`, `payout_account_ref` | Provider profile + economics. |
| `availability_slots` | `provider_id`, `start_at`, `end_at`, `is_booked bool` | For scheduled bookings (optional in MVP alongside "now"). |
| `bookings` | `customer_id`, `provider_id`, `slot_id` (nullable), `block_minutes` (15/30/45), `start_mode` (`now`/`scheduled`), `scheduled_at`, `price_block_cents`, `overage_per_min_cents`, `status` (`pending`/`confirmed`/`in_progress`/`completed`/`cancelled`), `payment_ref` | A purchase intent. |
| `sessions` | `booking_id`, `provider_id`, `customer_id`, `call_session_ref`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `elapsed_seconds`, `block_minutes`, `overage_minutes`, `total_price_cents`, `commission_cents`, `provider_earnings_cents`, `status` | The actual call + final accounting. |
| `payments` | `booking_id`, `customer_id`, `amount_cents`, `status` (`authorized`/`captured`/`refunded`/`failed`), `payment_ref` | Ledger row per booking. |
| `payouts` | `provider_id`, `period_start`, `period_end`, `amount_cents`, `status` (`scheduled`/`paid`), `scheduled_for` | Weekly aggregation (mock). |
| `reviews` | `session_id`, `customer_id`, `provider_id`, `rating` (1–5), `comment`, `tip_cents` | Updates provider rating; tip adds to earnings. |
| `reports` | `reporter_id`, `target_id`, `session_id`, `reason`, `status` (`open`/`reviewed`) | **Table only** for now (records in-app reports); moderation UI deferred (§12). |

**RLS summary:** customers read/write only their own `bookings`/`sessions`/`payments`/`reviews`; providers read their own `providers`/`sessions`/`payouts`; **public** reads only the public fields of `approved` providers; `admin` role reads/writes all. Privileged server actions use the Supabase service-role client.

---

## 5. Pricing & accounting logic (`lib/pricing.ts`)

Single source of truth. Pure, unit-tested functions. No pricing math anywhere else.

```ts
const COMMISSION = Number(process.env.PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE ?? "0.05");

// At booking: customer authorizes the block price.
priceForBlock(provider, blockMinutes) -> price_block_cents

// At session end:
overageMinutes = max(0, ceil((elapsedSeconds - blockMinutes*60) / 60))
totalCents     = price_block_cents + overageMinutes * overage_per_min_cents
commissionCents      = round(totalCents * COMMISSION)
providerEarningsCents = totalCents - commissionCents   // + any tip added later
```

Rules: round half-up to the nearest cent; a tip (from a review) is added to `provider_earnings_cents` and is **not** subject to commission; a no-show/early-cancel policy releases or partially captures the hold (define a simple rule: cancel ≥1h before scheduled = full release; in-progress end before block = still charge full block).

---

## 6. Screens & routes

Follow `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` for visual + interaction detail. Route map (App Router):

**Auth** — `/signin`, `/signup` (role chosen at sign-up: customer or provider).

**Customer**
- `/` — Welcome (marketing).
- `/browse` — Discover listeners (filters: topic, language, available-now, price; voice-intro players).
- `/listeners/[id]` — Listener profile (voice intro, bio, topics, reviews, "Talk now" / "Schedule").
- `/book/[providerId]` — Choose block (15/30/45) + now/scheduled; price summary; mock payment → `authorizeHold`.
- `/session/[id]` — Pre-call (waiting room) → in-call mock screen (count-up timer, mute, captions, end).
- `/session/[id]/summary` — Post-call: rating + optional tip + receipt.
- `/account` — Customer's bookings/history.

**Provider**
- `/provider/onboarding` — Audio-first, step-based: record voice intro (upload to Storage), topics, languages, prices, availability → initiate mock background check (status `pending`).
- `/provider/dashboard` — Big "Available now" toggle, upcoming sessions, weekly earnings, rating.
- `/provider/sessions` + `/provider/session/[id]` — Incoming request → accept → in-session (mirrors customer call screen) → summary.

**Admin**
- `/admin/providers` — Approval queue: list `pending` providers, view details + voice intro, **Approve / Reject / Suspend** (sets `status` and `bg_check_status`).

---

## 7. Key flows (server actions)

1. **Sign-up / role** → create `auth.users` + `profiles` row with chosen role; provider sign-up also creates a `providers` row (`status=pending`).
2. **Provider onboarding** → update `providers`, upload `voice_intro_path` to Storage, `backgroundCheck.initiate()` → `bg_check_status=pending`.
3. **Admin approval** → set `providers.status=approved`, `bg_check_status=clear` (or reject/suspend).
4. **Browse** → query `approved` providers with filters; signed URLs for voice intros.
5. **Booking** → validate slot/availability → create `booking` (`pending`) → `payments.authorizeHold(price_block)` → `booking.status=confirmed`, write `payments` row.
6. **Session start** → `calls.createSession()` → `session` (`in_progress`), `booking.status=in_progress`; render mock call; timer runs.
7. **Session end** → read elapsed → `pricing` computes overage/total/commission/earnings → `payments.capture(total)` → `recordProviderEarning()` → `session.status=completed`, `booking.status=completed` → route to summary.
8. **Review + tip** → create `review`, recompute `rating_avg`/`rating_count`, add tip to earnings.
9. **Weekly payouts (mock)** → `payments.runWeeklyPayouts()` aggregates per provider into `payouts`.

Every action: Zod-validate input, check the caller's role/ownership, return typed result, handle errors gracefully.

---

## 8. Folder structure

```
app/
  (marketing)/page.tsx                 # /
  (auth)/signin/  (auth)/signup/
  (customer)/browse/  listeners/[id]/  book/[providerId]/  session/[id]/  account/
  (provider)/provider/onboarding/  dashboard/  sessions/  session/[id]/
  (admin)/admin/providers/
  api/webhooks/payments/  api/webhooks/calls/   # for real adapters later
lib/
  integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/{interface,mock,real,index}.ts
  supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts
  db/queries.ts        validation/schemas.ts     pricing.ts     auth.ts
components/
  ui/                  # design-system primitives (Button, Field, Card, Dialog…)
  customer/  provider/ admin/  shared/
messages/en.json       # all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
supabase/migrations/*.sql   supabase/seed.sql
tests/                 # unit + component + e2e
CLAUDE.md   BUILD_PLAN.md   README.md   .env.example
```

---

## 9. Configuration (`.env.example`)

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock            # mock | real
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
# Real integrations (later, unused in mock mode):
# STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=  STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=  STRIPE_CONNECT_CLIENT_ID=
# ZOOM_MEETING_SDK_KEY=  ZOOM_MEETING_SDK_SECRET=  ZOOM_S2S_ACCOUNT_ID=  ZOOM_S2S_CLIENT_ID=  ZOOM_S2S_CLIENT_SECRET=
# CHECKR_API_KEY=
```

---

## 10. Accessibility (build-time requirements)

Treat as acceptance criteria, not aspiration:
- Semantic HTML, one logical heading order, landmarks; real `<button>`/`<a>`.
- **Keyboard-operable everywhere**, visible focus ring on every interactive element (never remove without a stronger replacement).
- All controls labeled (`aria-label`/associated `<label>`); icon-only buttons forbidden.
- No state by color alone — pair with text/icon.
- Live-region announcements for state changes (availability on/off, "call connected — timer started", booking confirmed).
- Body text ≥ 18px; layout survives 200% zoom; contrast AA (AAA on body).
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; no autoplaying audio.
- Persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" link on every page.
- Integrate **axe** checks into the component tests; a screen must pass before its milestone is "done".

---

## 11. Testing & quality

- **Unit (Vitest):** `lib/pricing.ts` (blocks, overage, commission, tips, rounding), each mock adapter, validation schemas.
- **Component (React Testing Library + axe):** core screens render, are keyboard-navigable, and pass a11y checks.
- **E2E (Playwright):** two happy paths — (a) customer browse → book → run mock session → rate; (b) provider onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.
- **Types:** TypeScript `strict`. **Lint:** ESLint + Prettier. CI runs typecheck + lint + tests.

---

## 12. Explicitly out of scope (this build)

Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr calls (mock only); native mobile apps; on-demand matching algorithm; **moderation/reporting UI** (the `reports` table and an in-app "Report a problem" button that writes to it are included as a minimal safety hook, but no admin moderation screen yet); subscriptions; insurance/benefits payer model. These are noted as fast-follows; design the schema and adapters so none require a rewrite.

---

## 13. Definition of done (whole build)

- All routes in §6 implemented and reachable; the customer and provider happy paths in §11 pass E2E.
- Integrations run in `mock` mode end-to-end with a seeded set of 6 providers; switching `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles and reaches clearly-marked `// TODO` stubs.
- All money via `lib/pricing.ts`; commission read from config; everything in integer cents.
- RLS enforced on every table; no service-role key on the client; no secrets in client bundles.
- Accessibility criteria in §10 met and checked by axe in tests.
- `README.md` documents setup, env, `supabase` migrate/seed, and how to swap a mock adapter for a real one.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

1	# Project Design Brief — Interactive Prototype
2	
3	**Product:** A marketplace where people pay to talk with, and be listened to by, professional companion listeners — all of whom are legally blind or visually impaired.
4	**Working name:** *(TBD — placeholder: “Heard”)*
5	**This document:** A paste-ready brief for **Claude** to generate a clickable, high-fidelity **interactive prototype** as a single-file artifact.
6	**Scope chosen:** Both sides, customer-led. **Visual direction:** Warm & trustworthy. **Market:** US. **Positioning:** Companionship & conversation — *non-clinical, never therapy.*
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. How to use this brief with Claude
11	
12	Paste this whole file into Claude and ask: *“Build this as a single-file React artifact (.jsx). Make every screen reachable and keyboard-navigable. Use only in-memory state.”* A ready-to-send prompt is in the last section. The **Technical constraints** section (§9) is mandatory — it reflects what actually runs in a Claude artifact.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Product context
17	
18	People are lonely at scale, and they already pay to be heard. This product channels that demand to a workforce the job market overlooks: blind and visually-impaired adults, who are often exceptional listeners and for whom remote, voice-only work removes the usual barriers. The customer buys a block of time to simply talk and be listened to. The provider earns dignified, flexible income.
19	
20	The product is **not therapy, coaching, or crisis support** — it is companionship and conversation. The prototype must reflect that framing in its copy and its safety affordances.
21	
22	The hero interaction is **voice**: customers discover listeners by hearing a short voice intro, and the session itself is an audio call. (In production, calls run on an embedded Zoom Meeting SDK; in the prototype, the call screen is a faithful *representation* — no real audio needed.)
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Target users
27	
28	**Customers (demand side)**
29	- Isolated older adults (often low-vision themselves — design for them too).
30	- Socially anxious adults who want low-stakes, judgment-free connection.
31	- Homebound or disabled people; people in grief, transition, or on night shifts; expats wanting conversation or language practice.
32	- Emotional state on arrival: often lonely, sometimes vulnerable. The UI must feel **calm, warm, safe, and unhurried** — never gamified, addictive, or salesy.
33	
34	**Providers (supply side)**
35	- Legally blind / visually-impaired adults working from home with a **screen reader** (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver) and a headset.
36	- They are the reason accessibility is not a feature here — it is the foundation. **If a blind person cannot operate a screen end-to-end by ear and keyboard, that screen is broken.**
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 3. Design goals & principles
41	
42	1. **Accessibility is the product, not a layer.** Target WCAG 2.2 AA as a floor; aim for AAA contrast on body text. Everything operable by keyboard and screen reader.
43	2. **Warm, human, trustworthy.** Soft and reassuring, like a kind friend — not clinical, not a dating app, not a slot machine.
44	3. **Voice-first.** Lead with listening: voice-intro players in discovery, audio cues, captions/transcripts available.
45	4. **Dignity over pity.** Present providers as skilled listeners who happen to be blind. Never “help the blind” charity framing. Their blindness is part of an authentic story, not the pitch.
46	5. **Calm, low-pressure pacing.** Generous space, large type, few choices per screen, no dark patterns, no urgency timers pushing purchases.
47	6. **Safety in plain sight.** A persistent, gentle “This is companionship, not therapy” note and an easy path to crisis resources — without making the space feel grim.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 4. Information architecture & flows
52	
53	The **customer journey is the spine**; key **provider screens** branch off. Provide a simple top-level toggle in the prototype (e.g., “View as: Customer / Listener”) so reviewers can switch perspectives.
54	
55	```
56	CUSTOMER:  Welcome → Browse listeners → Listener profile → Book session
57	           → Pre-call (waiting room) → In-call → Post-call (rate & rebook)
58	
59	LISTENER:  Accessible onboarding → Dashboard (availability & earnings)
60	           → Incoming request → In-session → Session summary
61	```
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 5. Screen-by-screen specification
66	
67	For each screen: purpose, key components, states, and what is clickable in the prototype.
68	
69	### Customer · C1 — Welcome
70	- **Purpose:** Warm first impression; state the value in one human sentence.
71	- **Components:** Soft hero (“Someone to talk to, whenever you need it.”), one-line subtext, a single primary CTA **“Find someone to talk to”**, a quiet secondary link “How it works”, a subtle trust line (“Real people. Great listeners. Always judgment-free.”).
72	- **Clickable:** Primary CTA → C2.
73	
74	### Customer · C2 — Browse listeners
75	- **Purpose:** Discover a listener by *voice* and vibe, not looks.
76	- **Components:**
77	  - Filter row: *Available now* toggle, interests/topics chips (e.g., “everyday chat”, “grief”, “sports”, “books”, “just listen”), language, price.
78	  - **Listener cards** (grid/list): avatar, first name, **▶ voice-intro play button** (the focal element), 2–3 interest tags, languages, star rating, simple price (e.g., “$0.80/min” or “$24 / 30 min”), and an availability dot with a **text label** (never color alone).
79	- **States:** available / busy / scheduled-only; playing vs. idle voice intro.
80	- **Clickable:** A card or its name → C3; play button toggles a simulated “Playing…” state.
81	
82	### Customer · C3 — Listener profile
83	- **Purpose:** Build trust and choose.
84	- **Components:** Larger avatar + name, **prominent voice-intro player**, short bio in their own voice/words, “What I love talking about” tags, languages, ratings + a few warm review snippets, availability (Now / next slots), and two CTAs: **“Talk now”** (if available) and **“Schedule a time.”**
85	- **Clickable:** Either CTA → C4.
86	
87	### Customer · C4 — Book a session
88	- **Purpose:** Choose length + time, confirm payment (mock).
89	- **Components:** Duration selector as friendly blocks — **15 / 30 / 45 min** (note: production sessions cap near 40 min; keep blocks at/under that). Time = “Start now” or a simple slot picker. Clear price summary. Mock payment (“•••• 4242”). A small reassurance line: *“You’re in control — leave any time. This is companionship, not medical or mental-health care.”* Primary CTA **“Confirm & connect.”**
90	- **Clickable:** Confirm → C5.
91	
92	### Customer · C5 — Pre-call (waiting room)
93	- **Purpose:** Calm the transition.
94	- **Components:** “Connecting you with **[Name]**…” with a gentle animated indicator (respect reduced-motion), a one-line etiquette/safety note, a mic-check affordance, and **“Cancel.”**
95	- **Clickable:** Auto-advance (or a “Join” button) → C6; Cancel → C3.
96	
97	### Customer · C6 — In-call (audio-first)
98	- **Purpose:** A serene space to talk. This represents the embedded Zoom call.
99	- **Components:** Large listener avatar with a soft **audio waveform/“speaking” indicator**, the listener’s name, a **session timer counting up**, and a compact control bar: **Mute**, **Captions** toggle, **End**. Optional: a “captions” panel with sample text. No clutter, no video pressure.
100	- **States:** timer ticking; mute on/off; captions on/off.
101	- **Clickable:** End → C7; controls toggle visibly.
102	
103	### Customer · C7 — Post-call
104	- **Purpose:** Close warmly, capture feedback, encourage return.
105	- **Components:** “How was your conversation with **[Name]**?” → simple star/emoji rating, an **optional tip** (Skip is equally prominent), a short free-text “Say thanks” field, a receipt summary, and CTAs **“Book again”** and **“Back to listeners.”**
106	- **Clickable:** Both CTAs route back (C3 / C2).
107	
108	### Listener · P1 — Accessible onboarding
109	- **Purpose:** Show the audio-first, screen-reader-first provider setup. **This screen is the accessibility showpiece.**
110	- **Components:** A clear, single-column, step-based flow (one task per screen), with very large targets and obvious focus:
111	  1. Record your **voice intro** (record / re-record / play — all clearly labeled).
112	  2. Choose **topics you enjoy** and **languages** (large checkable chips).
113	  3. Set **availability** and your **rate.**
114	  4. **Verification status** (ID + background check) shown as plain text steps.
115	- **Requirements to make visible in the brief:** visible focus ring on every control, explicit text labels (no icon-only buttons), step “3 of 4” text progress, and an always-available “Need help? Call us” path.
116	- **Clickable:** Step nav (Back/Next) → P2 on completion.
117	
118	### Listener · P2 — Dashboard
119	- **Purpose:** At-a-glance control of work.
120	- **Components:** A big, unmistakable **“Available now” toggle** (with text state “You’re available” / “You’re offline”), today’s upcoming sessions, this week’s **earnings**, rating, and a recent-activity list. High contrast, large type, minimal density.
121	- **Clickable:** Toggle flips state; an incoming request can be simulated → P3.
122	
123	### Listener · P3 — Incoming request & in-session
124	- **Purpose:** Accept and run a session.
125	- **Components:** Incoming card (“**[Customer]** would like to talk — 30 min”) with **Accept / Decline** (both clearly labeled, generous size). On accept → an in-session view mirroring C6 (timer, mute, captions, end) plus a discreet **“Report / End for safety”** control.
126	- **Clickable:** Accept → in-session; End → P4.
127	
128	### Listener · P4 — Session summary
129	- **Purpose:** Close the loop for the provider.
130	- **Components:** Duration, earnings from this session, optional note from customer, and **“Back to dashboard.”**
131	
132	---
133	
134	## 6. Visual design direction — *Warm & trustworthy*
135	
136	**Mood:** soft daylight, warm paper, calm and human. Think “a sunlit living room,” not “a hospital” or “a tech dashboard.”
137	
138	### Color tokens (verify all text pairings ≥ 4.5:1; aim 7:1 for body)
139	| Token | Hex | Use |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| `bg` | `#FBF7F2` | Warm off-white page background |
142	| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | Cards, sheets |
143	| `ink` | `#2A2622` | Primary text (near-black, warm) |
144	| `ink-soft` | `#6B6259` | Secondary text |
145	| `primary` | `#136F63` | Calm teal — trust; primary buttons (white text) |
146	| `primary-dark` | `#0E5249` | Hover/active |
147	| `accent` | `#E08A3C` | Warm amber — gentle highlights, tips, warmth |
148	| `success` | `#2E7D5B` | Available / positive (always paired with text/icon) |
149	| `alert` | `#B23A2E` | Errors / safety (paired with text/icon) |
150	| `border` | `#ECE3D8` | Hairlines, dividers |
151	| `focus` | `#1B6FB0` | High-visibility focus ring (3px, never removed) |
152	
153	> Never signal state with color alone — always add a text label or icon.
154	
155	### Typography
156	- **Family:** humanist sans — Inter / Nunito / system-ui. Friendly, highly legible.
157	- **Base size:** **18px** body minimum (this audience skews older/low-vision). Line-height ~1.6.
158	- **Scale:** body 18 · large body 20 · h3 24 · h2 30 · h1 38 (responsive). Generous, never cramped.
159	- Support browser text-zoom to 200% without breaking layout.
160	
161	### Form & spacing
162	- 8px spacing grid; generous whitespace and breathing room.
163	- **Tap targets ≥ 48px.** Buttons large and obvious; primary actions full-width on mobile.
164	- Rounded corners (cards ~16px, buttons ~12px); soft, low shadows; subtle warm borders.
165	- Icons: **lucide-react**, always paired with a text label (no icon-only controls).
166	- Imagery: warm, candid, diverse; avatars are illustrative. Avoid stocky “sad lonely person” tropes and avoid pity imagery of blindness.
167	
168	### Layout
169	- **Mobile-first**, single-column, responsive up to a comfortable desktop max-width. Render the prototype inside a phone-width frame by default, but it must reflow gracefully wider.
170	
171	---
172	
173	## 7. Accessibility requirements (non-negotiable)
174	
175	- **WCAG 2.2 AA** minimum; AAA contrast on body text where feasible.
176	- Full **keyboard operability**; logical tab order; **visible focus ring** on every interactive element (never `outline:none` without a stronger replacement).
177	- **Semantic structure:** real headings, landmarks, `button`/`a` elements, `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on all controls (especially icon-bearing ones and the voice-intro player).
178	- **Screen-reader friendly:** meaningful labels, live-region announcements for state changes (e.g., “Now available”, “Call connected, timer started”), no information conveyed by color or position alone.
179	- **Voice/audio:** every voice intro and the call screen have text equivalents; captions toggle present; controls labeled for speech.
180	- **Motion:** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; no essential info in animation; no auto-playing audio.
181	- **Forms:** labels tied to inputs, clear error text, large hit areas.
182	- **Safety affordance:** a persistent, calm “Companionship, not therapy — if you’re in crisis, find support” link reachable from every screen.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## 8. Voice & microcopy
187	
188	Warm, plain, short, dignified. Speak like a kind, steady friend. Examples:
189	- Welcome: *“Someone to talk to, whenever you need it.”*
190	- Reassurance: *“No pressure, no judgment. Talk for as long as you like.”*
191	- Safety: *“This is companionship, not medical or mental-health care. If you’re in crisis, we’ll help you find support.”*
192	- Provider availability: *“You’re available — new requests can reach you.”*
193	- Empty/quiet states: *“No sessions yet today. When someone needs an ear, you’ll see them here.”*
194	
195	Avoid: clinical jargon, urgency (“Only 2 left!”), pity (“Support the blind”), or hype.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 9. Technical constraints (for the Claude artifact) — mandatory
200	
201	- **Single file, React, default export** (`.jsx`). No multi-file projects.
202	- **Styling:** Tailwind **core utility classes only** (no config, no arbitrary values that rely on a compiler where avoidable). Use the palette above via close Tailwind equivalents or inline style for exact hex.
203	- **State:** `useState` / `useReducer` only. **No `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`** (unsupported in artifacts) — keep all data in memory.
204	- **Icons:** `lucide-react`. **Charts (if any):** `recharts`.
205	- **No external network calls, no real audio.** Simulate playing/connecting/timer with state and `setInterval`.
206	- **Mock data inline** (see model below). Provide ~6 sample listeners with varied names, tags, languages, ratings, and availability.
207	- **Navigation:** simple in-memory screen router (a `screen` state variable + setter); include the **Customer / Listener** perspective toggle.
208	- Mobile-first; works in a narrow frame and reflows wider; all interactions keyboard-reachable.
209	
210	**Suggested data model**
211	```js
212	// Listener
213	{ id, firstName, avatarColor, intro: "text shown as the 'voice intro' transcript",
214	  tags: ["everyday chat","grief"], languages: ["English","Spanish"],
215	  rating: 4.9, reviews: 128, pricePerMin: 0.8, status: "available"|"busy"|"scheduled" }
216	
217	// Booking
218	{ listenerId, durationMin: 30, startMode: "now"|"scheduled", priceTotal }
219	
220	// Session (runtime)
221	{ listenerId, elapsedSec, muted: false, captionsOn: false }
222	```
223	
224	---
225	
226	## 10. Prototype interaction behavior
227	
228	- Every primary CTA navigates per §4. Provide a persistent, accessible **back** affordance.
229	- Voice-intro **play** buttons toggle a visible “Playing…” state (and announce it for screen readers).
230	- Booking computes and shows the **price** from duration × rate.
231	- In-call/in-session: timer **counts up** via `setInterval`; **Mute** and **Captions** visibly toggle; **End** routes to the summary/rating.
232	- Listener **“Available now”** toggle flips a clearly labeled state and can surface a simulated incoming request.
233	- Respect reduced motion; keep all transitions gentle.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 11. Acceptance criteria (definition of done)
238	
239	- [ ] All 11 screens (C1–C7, P1–P4) are reachable and the Customer/Listener toggle works.
240	- [ ] Entire prototype is operable by **keyboard alone**, with a visible focus ring throughout.
241	- [ ] No state is conveyed by color alone; all controls have text or `aria-label`.
242	- [ ] Body text ≥ 18px; layout survives 200% zoom; contrast meets AA (AAA on body).
243	- [ ] Voice-intro players, captions toggle, and the “not therapy / crisis” affordance are present.
244	- [ ] In-call timer runs; mute/captions/end and the availability toggle all function.
245	- [ ] Look and feel matches the warm, trustworthy palette and typography; calm, uncluttered, no dark patterns.
246	
247	---
248	
249	## 12. Out of scope (for this prototype)
250	
251	Real audio/video, real payments, real auth, native mobile apps, on-demand matching algorithms, admin/moderation tooling, and the actual Zoom embed. These are production concerns; the prototype only needs to *represent* the call convincingly.
252	
253	---
254	
255	## 13. Ready-to-send prompt for Claude
256	
257	> Build a single-file React artifact (`.jsx`, default export) for an interactive, high-fidelity prototype of a companionship marketplace where every listener is blind or visually impaired. Implement these screens with an in-memory screen router and a Customer/Listener perspective toggle: **Customer** — Welcome, Browse listeners, Listener profile, Book session, Pre-call, In-call, Post-call; **Listener** — Accessible onboarding, Dashboard, Incoming request/In-session, Session summary. Follow the warm, trustworthy palette and typography, 18px+ body text, tap targets ≥48px, mobile-first. Make it **fully keyboard-operable with visible focus rings**, semantic and screen-reader-labeled, with no color-only state, captions toggles, voice-intro players (simulated), a counting-up call timer (`setInterval`), and a persistent “companionship, not therapy / crisis support” link. Use Tailwind core classes, `lucide-react` icons, `useState` only (no localStorage), and inline mock data for ~6 listeners. Keep it calm and uncluttered — no dark patterns, respect reduced motion.

- **Purpose:** At-a-glance control of work.
- **Components:** A big, unmistakable **“Available now” toggle** (with text state “You’re available” / “You’re offline”), today’s upcoming sessions, this week’s **earnings**, rating, and a recent-activity list. High contrast, large type, minimal density.
- **Clickable:** Toggle flips state; an incoming request can be simulated → P3.

### Listener · P3 — Incoming request & in-session
- **Purpose:** Accept and run a session.
- **Components:** Incoming card (“**[Customer]** would like to talk — 30 min”) with **Accept / Decline** (both clearly labeled, generous size). On accept → an in-session view mirroring C6 (timer, mute, captions, end) plus a discreet **“Report / End for safety”** control.
- **Clickable:** Accept → in-session; End → P4.

### Listener · P4 — Session summary
- **Purpose:** Close the loop for the provider.
- **Components:** Duration, earnings from this session, optional note from customer, and **“Back to dashboard.”**

---

## 6. Visual design direction — *Warm & trustworthy*

**Mood:** soft daylight, warm paper, calm and human. Think “a sunlit living room,” not “a hospital” or “a tech dashboard.”

### Color tokens (verify all text pairings ≥ 4.5:1; aim 7:1 for body)
| Token | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` | `#FBF7F2` | Warm off-white page background |
| `surface` | `#FFFFFF` | Cards, sheets |
| `ink` | `#2A2622` | Primary text (near-black, warm) |
| `ink-soft` | `#6B6259` | Secondary text |
| `primary` | `#136F63` | Calm teal — trust; primary buttons (white text) |
| `primary-dark` | `#0E5249` | Hover/active |
| `accent` | `#E08A3C` | Warm amber — gentle highlights, tips, warmth |
| `success` | `#2E7D5B` | Available / positive (always paired with text/icon) |
| `alert` | `#B23A2E` | Errors / safety (paired with text/icon) |
| `border` | `#ECE3D8` | Hairlines, dividers |
| `focus` | `#1B6FB0` | High-visibility focus ring (3px, never removed) |

> Never signal state with color alone — always add a text label or icon.

### Typography
- **Family:** humanist sans — Inter / Nunito / system-ui. Friendly, highly legible.
- **Base size:** **18px** body minimum (this audience skews older/low-vision). Line-height ~1.6.
- **Scale:** body 18 · large body 20 · h3 24 · h2 30 · h1 38 (responsive). Generous, never cramped.
- Support browser text-zoom to 200% without breaking layout.

### Form & spacing
- 8px spacing grid; generous whitespace and breathing room.
- **Tap targets ≥ 48px.** Buttons large and obvious; primary actions full-width on mobile.
- Rounded corners (cards ~16px, buttons ~12px); soft, low shadows; subtle warm borders.
- Icons: **lucide-react**, always paired with a text label (no icon-only controls).
- Imagery: warm, candid, diverse; avatars are illustrative. Avoid stocky “sad lonely person” tropes and avoid pity imagery of blindness.

### Layout
- **Mobile-first**, single-column, responsive up to a comfortable desktop max-width. Render the prototype inside a phone-width frame by default, but it must reflow gracefully wider.

---

## 7. Accessibility requirements (non-negotiable)

- **WCAG 2.2 AA** minimum; AAA contrast on body text where feasible.
- Full **keyboard operability**; logical tab order; **visible focus ring** on every interactive element (never `outline:none` without a stronger replacement).
- **Semantic structure:** real headings, landmarks, `button`/`a` elements, `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on all controls (especially icon-bearing ones and the voice-intro player).
- **Screen-reader friendly:** meaningful labels, live-region announcements for state changes (e.g., “Now available”, “Call connected, timer started”), no information conveyed by color or position alone.
- **Voice/audio:** every voice intro and the call screen have text equivalents; captions toggle present; controls labeled for speech.
- **Motion:** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; no essential info in animation; no auto-playing audio.
- **Forms:** labels tied to inputs, clear error text, large hit areas.
- **Safety affordance:** a persistent, calm “Companionship, not therapy — if you’re in crisis, find support” link reachable from every screen.

---

## 8. Voice & microcopy

Warm, plain, short, dignified. Speak like a kind, steady friend. Examples:
- Welcome: *“Someone to talk to, whenever you need it.”*
- Reassurance: *“No pressure, no judgment. Talk for as long as you like.”*
- Safety: *“This is companionship, not medical or mental-health care. If you’re in crisis, we’ll help you find support.”*
- Provider availability: *“You’re available — new requests can reach you.”*
- Empty/quiet states: *“No sessions yet today. When someone needs an ear, you’ll see them here.”*

Avoid: clinical jargon, urgency (“Only 2 left!”), pity (“Support the blind”), or hype.

---

## 9. Technical constraints (for the Claude artifact) — mandatory

- **Single file, React, default export** (`.jsx`). No multi-file projects.
- **Styling:** Tailwind **core utility classes only** (no config, no arbitrary values that rely on a compiler where avoidable). Use the palette above via close Tailwind equivalents or inline style for exact hex.
- **State:** `useState` / `useReducer` only. **No `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`** (unsupported in artifacts) — keep all data in memory.
- **Icons:** `lucide-react`. **Charts (if any):** `recharts`.
- **No external network calls, no real audio.** Simulate playing/connecting/timer with state and `setInterval`.
- **Mock data inline** (see model below). Provide ~6 sample listeners with varied names, tags, languages, ratings, and availability.
- **Navigation:** simple in-memory screen router (a `screen` state variable + setter); include the **Customer / Listener** perspective toggle.
- Mobile-first; works in a narrow frame and reflows wider; all interactions keyboard-reachable.

**Suggested data model**
```js
// Listener
{ id, firstName, avatarColor, intro: "text shown as the 'voice intro' transcript",
  tags: ["everyday chat","grief"], languages: ["English","Spanish"],
  rating: 4.9, reviews: 128, pricePerMin: 0.8, status: "available"|"busy"|"scheduled" }

// Booking
{ listenerId, durationMin: 30, startMode: "now"|"scheduled", priceTotal }

// Session (runtime)
{ listenerId, elapsedSec, muted: false, captionsOn: false }
```

---

## 10. Prototype interaction behavior

- Every primary CTA navigates per §4. Provide a persistent, accessible **back** affordance.
- Voice-intro **play** buttons toggle a visible “Playing…” state (and announce it for screen readers).
- Booking computes and shows the **price** from duration × rate.
- In-call/in-session: timer **counts up** via `setInterval`; **Mute** and **Captions** visibly toggle; **End** routes to the summary/rating.
- Listener **“Available now”** toggle flips a clearly labeled state and can surface a simulated incoming request.
- Respect reduced motion; keep all transitions gentle.

---

## 11. Acceptance criteria (definition of done)

- [ ] All 11 screens (C1–C7, P1–P4) are reachable and the Customer/Listener toggle works.
- [ ] Entire prototype is operable by **keyboard alone**, with a visible focus ring throughout.
- [ ] No state is conveyed by color alone; all controls have text or `aria-label`.
- [ ] Body text ≥ 18px; layout survives 200% zoom; contrast meets AA (AAA on body).
- [ ] Voice-intro players, captions toggle, and the “not therapy / crisis” affordance are present.
- [ ] In-call timer runs; mute/captions/end and the availability toggle all function.
- [ ] Look and feel matches the warm, trustworthy palette and typography; calm, uncluttered, no dark patterns.

---

## 12. Out of scope (for this prototype)

Real audio/video, real payments, real auth, native mobile apps, on-demand matching algorithms, admin/moderation tooling, and the actual Zoom embed. These are production concerns; the prototype only needs to *represent* the call convincingly.

---

## 13. Ready-to-send prompt for Claude

> Build a single-file React artifact (`.jsx`, default export) for an interactive, high-fidelity prototype of a companionship marketplace where every listener is blind or visually impaired. Implement these screens with an in-memory screen router and a Customer/Listener perspective toggle: **Customer** — Welcome, Browse listeners, Listener profile, Book session, Pre-call, In-call, Post-call; **Listener** — Accessible onboarding, Dashboard, Incoming request/In-session, Session summary. Follow the warm, trustworthy palette and typography, 18px+ body text, tap targets ≥48px, mobile-first. Make it **fully keyboard-operable with visible focus rings**, semantic and screen-reader-labeled, with no color-only state, captions toggles, voice-intro players (simulated), a counting-up call timer (`setInterval`), and a persistent “companionship, not therapy / crisis support” link. Use Tailwind core classes, `lucide-react` icons, `useState` only (no localStorage), and inline mock data for ~6 listeners. Keep it calm and uncluttered — no dark patterns, respect reduced motion.

## ICONOGRAPHY

- **System:** **Lucide** (the `lucide-react` set, matching the brief). Clean, rounded, **outline** icons at a consistent ~2px stroke — friendly without being childish, and they sit naturally beside Nunito's rounded terminals.
- **Delivery:** In React/production use `lucide-react`. In static HTML (this system's preview cards and the HTML mirror of the kit) Lucide is linked from CDN (`unpkg.com/lucide@latest`) and rendered with `lucide.createIcons()`. There is **no custom icon font or SVG sprite** — none existed in the source brief, and Lucide is the specified set, so it is used directly (not substituted).
- **Rules:** Icons are **always paired with a visible text label** — there are **no icon-only controls** anywhere (a hard accessibility requirement; icon-only buttons are broken for screen-reader and low-vision users). Decorative icons get `aria-hidden`; meaningful ones get an adjacent label or `aria-label`.
- **Common glyphs:** `play` / `pause` (voice intro), `mic` / `mic-off` (mute), `captions`, `phone` / `phone-off` (join/end), `circle` + text (availability), `shield` / `life-buoy` (safety), `star` (rating), `chevron-left` (back), `check` (selected).
- **Emoji as icons:** not used (see Content Fundamentals).
- **Unicode as icons:** avoided; Lucide covers the set.

---

## CAVEATS

- **Fonts via CDN.** Lora + Nunito Sans are loaded from Google Fonts, not bundled as local files (binary font fetching wasn't available in this environment). For fully offline/production use, download the `.woff2` files into `fonts/` and swap the `@import` for `@font-face`.
- **No real product to mirror.** With no codebase/Figma, the UI kit is a faithful build of the brief's spec rather than a recreation of shipped screens.

# Build Plan — "Heard"

## Context

We're building **Heard**: a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion
listeners who are all legally blind or visually impaired. Non-clinical companionship — never
therapy. The product's whole point is accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body contrast) and
the dignity of providers.

The working directory is **empty** (greenfield). I have the full source of truth:
- `SPEC.md` — architecture, data model, adapter pattern, pricing, routes, flows.
- `BUILD_PLAN.md` — milestones M0→M9.
- `CLAUDE.md` — golden rules (a11y, adapters-only, integer cents, RLS everywhere, validate at boundary, server-first, i18n copy, safety framing).
- Design brief + design system: exact color/type tokens (`colors_and_type.css`), voice/microcopy rules, and a working prototype (`ui.jsx`, `data.jsx`, 11 screens) to match the visual language.

**Decisions locked with you:** (1) **Local Supabase CLI** — real SQL migrations + RLS + seed,
runnable via `supabase db reset`. (2) **Milestone checkpoints** — build M0, stop and show it runs,
then continue milestone by milestone.

**Toolchain gap found:** Node 26 / npm 11 / git / Homebrew are present, but the **Supabase CLI and
any container runtime (Docker/Colima/Podman) are missing**. Local Supabase needs a container runtime.
M0 therefore includes a headless install via Homebrew (`supabase` + `colima` + `docker` CLI) — no
Docker Desktop GUI required.

The reference material lives under `_refs/` (extracted from the two zips). It is reference only and
will not ship; I'll keep it out of the app and gitignore it (or remove it before handoff).

---

## Stack & conventions (apply on every milestone)

- Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript `strict` · Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage) · Tailwind · Zod · Vitest + RTL + Playwright.
- Design tokens from `colors_and_type.css` become Tailwind theme + CSS vars in `globals.css`. Lora (display) + Nunito Sans (body), 18px body floor, ≥48px tap targets, 3px `#1B6FB0` focus ring never removed.
- All external services through adapters only (`getPayments/getCalls/getBackgroundCheck`); never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly.
- All money integer cents; all pricing math only in `lib/pricing.ts`; commission from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`.
- RLS on every table; service-role key server-only. Zod-validate + role/ownership-check every server action.
- All user-facing copy via `messages/en.json`. Persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" affordance on every page.
- Each milestone ends green: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, and an **axe** pass on any new screen.

---

## This session = M0 only (then checkpoint)

**Goal of M0:** a user can sign up / sign in as customer or provider, role persists, every UI
primitive passes axe, app shell + safety affordance render, CI scripts green.

### M0.0 — Toolchain (one-time, needs your approval to install)
- `brew install supabase/tap/supabase` (Supabase CLI).
- `brew install colima docker` (headless container runtime + docker client), then `colima start`.
- Verify `supabase --version` and `docker info` work. (Colima pulls a small Linux VM image on first start — a few minutes.)

### M0.1 — Scaffold
- `create-next-app` (App Router, TS, Tailwind, ESLint) into the working dir.
- Add Prettier, Vitest + RTL + `jest-axe`, Playwright. `package.json` scripts: `dev/build/lint/typecheck/test/test:e2e`.
- `tsconfig` strict; ESLint + Prettier configs.
- GitHub Actions CI: typecheck + lint + test. `git init` + first commit.
- `.gitignore` includes `_refs/`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.next`.

### M0.2 — Supabase wiring
- `supabase init`. `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts` (SSR `@supabase/ssr`: browser client, server client w/ cookies, middleware session refresh).
- `.env.example` exactly per SPEC §9 (URL, anon, service-role, `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`, `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard`, commented real-integration keys). Write local `.env.local` from `supabase start` output.
- Minimal `profiles` migration here (full data model is M1) so sign-up can create a profile row and auth works end-to-end this milestone.

### M0.3 — Design tokens + i18n
- `app/globals.css`: import Lora + Nunito Sans; port every `--token` from `colors_and_type.css`; semantic defaults (body bg/color/font, heading font, universal `:focus-visible` ring, reduced-motion block).
- `tailwind.config.ts`: map tokens to theme (colors, fontFamily, radii, shadows, spacing) so utilities and tokens agree.
- `messages/en.json` + tiny `lib/i18n.ts` `t()` helper (typed key lookup). Seed with microcopy verbatim from the design README (hero, trust line, reassurance, safety line, availability states, empty states). **No hard-coded UI strings after this.**

### M0.4 — UI primitives (`components/ui/`), accessible by construction
Ported from the prototype's `ui.jsx` to typed React + Tailwind/tokens:
`Button` (primary/amber/ghost/danger/quiet, icon+label, ≥48px), `Field`/`Input`, `Select`,
`Card`, `Dialog` (focus-trap, Esc, scrim), `Toast` + live-region announcer, `Tag`/`Chip`
(`aria-pressed`, check icon), `Avatar` (initial tile), `FocusRing` util, plus product primitives
`Availability` (icon+text, never color alone), `VoicePlayer` (simulated, labeled), `SafetyNote`.
Icons via `lucide-react`, always with text/`aria-label` — no icon-only controls.

### M0.5 — Auth + app shell
- `/signin`, `/signup` (server actions + Zod). Sign-up has **role selection** (customer/provider). On sign-up: create `profiles` row; provider also creates a `providers` row `status=pending` (provider insert via service-role server action).
- `lib/auth.ts`: `getUser()`, `getProfile()`, `requireRole()`.
- App shell: header/nav + persistent SafetyNote affordance; route groups `(marketing)/(auth)/(customer)/(provider)/(admin)`; middleware redirects by auth/role. Crisis-support dialog reachable from the affordance.

### M0.6 — Tests + green gate
- Unit: `t()` helper, role-selection schema.
- Component + **axe**: each `components/ui` primitive, `/signin`, `/signup`.
- Run `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`. Smoke-run `dev`.

**M0 done when:** sign up/in as either role works, role persists in `profiles`/`providers`, every
primitive + auth screen passes axe, CI scripts pass locally. → **Stop, show you it runs, get sign-off for M1.**

---

## Remaining milestones (later sessions, same checkpoint cadence)

- **M1** — Full data model migrations + RLS for all SPEC §4 tables; `seed.sql` (6 providers + admin + customer); `lib/db/queries.ts` + `lib/validation/schemas.ts`. Done when `supabase db reset` applies clean and RLS is verified.
- **M2** — Integration adapters (payments/calls/background-check): `interface/mock/real/index`; `lib/pricing.ts` pure (blocks, overage, 5% commission, tips, half-up). Unit tests cover every mock + all pricing cases.
- **M3** — Provider side: audio-first `/provider/onboarding` (voice intro → Storage, topics/languages, prices, availability, `backgroundCheck.initiate()`), `/provider/dashboard` (Available-now toggle, sessions, earnings, rating). Keyboard/SR-verified.
- **M4** — Admin `/admin/providers` approval queue (approve/reject/suspend), role-guarded.
- **M5** — Customer discovery + booking: `/`, `/browse` (filters + voice players), `/listeners/[id]`, `/book/[providerId]` → `authorizeHold` + `booking` confirmed.
- **M6** — Session lifecycle: `/session/[id]` pre-call → mock call (count-up timer, mute, captions, end), provider mirror; on end → pricing → `capture` → `session` completed.
- **M7** — `/session/[id]/summary` rating + optional tip + receipt; weekly mock payouts; payout history.
- **M8** — Full a11y + visual polish pass (SPEC §10): focus order, live regions, 200% zoom, reduced motion, contrast; safety affordance + minimal report hook on every page.
- **M9** — Tests/docs/handoff: unit + component + 2 Playwright E2E happy paths; `README.md`; verify `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to TODO stubs.

---

## Verification (M0)

1. `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test` → all green; axe assertions pass for every primitive + `/signin` + `/signup`.
2. `supabase start` up; `npm run dev`; in browser: sign up as **customer** → `profiles.role=customer`; sign up as **provider** → `profiles.role=provider` + `providers` row `status=pending`; sign out / sign in works; middleware blocks unauthed routes.
3. Manual keyboard-only pass of `/signup`: visible focus ring on every control, role selection operable, no icon-only buttons.
4. SafetyNote affordance visible on every rendered page; crisis dialog opens and is focus-trapped.

## Notes / risks
- Colima first-start downloads a VM image (a few minutes); if you'd rather not install a runtime, the fallback is the "defer DB" mode — but you chose local Supabase, so M0.0 installs it.
- `_refs/` is reference only; gitignored, never imported by app code.

input.content:
# Heard

A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with — and be listened to by —
professional companion listeners, all of whom are legally blind or visually
impaired. **Companionship and conversation, not therapy.** Accessibility is the
product, not a layer.

See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for the full build spec, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
the conventions every change follows, and [`BUILD_PLAN.md`](BUILD_PLAN.md) for
the milestone plan. (A fuller README — including how to swap a mock adapter for
a real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr integration — lands in M9.)

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth +
Storage) · Tailwind v4 · Zod · Vitest + Testing Library + `jest-axe` ·
Playwright. External services (payments, calls, background checks) are reached
only through adapters and run in **mock** mode by default.

## Prerequisites

- Node 20+ and npm.
- A local container runtime + the Supabase CLI. On macOS without Docker Desktop,
  a headless setup works:

  ```sh
  brew install supabase/tap/supabase colima docker
  colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
  ```

  Colima exposes its Docker socket at `~/.colima/default/docker.sock`. If the
  Supabase/Docker CLIs can't find it, export:

  ```sh
  export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"
  ```

## Setup

```sh
npm install
supabase start                 # applies migrations in supabase/migrations/
supabase status -o env         # copy the keys below into .env.local
```

Create `.env.local` (see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) using the values from
`supabase status`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<ANON_KEY>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<SERVICE_ROLE_KEY>
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
```

Then:

```sh
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

> Local note: this project disables Supabase's `analytics` (Vector) container in
> `supabase/config.toml` because it bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's
> virtiofs mount doesn't support. Re-enable it on Docker Desktop or in CI.

## Scripts

```sh
npm run dev          # local dev
npm run build        # production build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
npm run test         # vitest (unit + component, incl. axe a11y checks)
npm run test:e2e     # playwright (E2E suites land in M9)
npm run db:reset     # supabase db reset (re-applies migrations + seed)
```

## Database types

`lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is generated from the live schema. Regenerate
after any migration:

```sh
supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public > lib/supabase/database.types.ts
```

## Status

**M0 complete** — foundation + auth: design tokens, accessible UI primitives,
email+password auth with customer/provider role selection (role persisted via a
`profiles`/`providers` trigger), RLS, the app shell, and the persistent
"companionship, not therapy / crisis support" affordance. Up next: **M1** — the
full data model, RLS, and seed.

The Heard app uses a **local Supabase CLI** stack on a **Colima** container runtime (no Docker Desktop installed).

**Why:** the user chose local Supabase; Docker Desktop wasn't present, so Colima + the docker CLI were installed via Homebrew.

**How to apply:**
- Start the runtime: `colima start` (already configured `--cpu 2 --memory 4`).
- Supabase/Docker CLI commands need the Colima socket: `export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"`.
- `supabase start` then exposes the API at `http://127.0.0.1:54321`; get keys with `supabase status -o env` and put them in `.env.local` (gitignored).
- The **analytics (Vector) container is disabled** in `supabase/config.toml` (`[analytics] enabled = false`) because it bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's virtiofs mount rejects. Don't re-enable it locally.
- The Next app talks to Supabase over HTTP (54321); it does NOT need DOCKER_HOST — only the supabase CLI does.

name: supabase-ssr-version
description: "@supabase/ssr must be 0.10+ in Heard or typed queries resolve to never"
metadata:
  type: project
---

In Heard, `@supabase/ssr` must be **0.10.x or newer**. The scaffold pulled 0.5.2, which is too old for `@supabase/supabase-js` 2.107: the `Database` generic did not flow through `createServerClient<Database>`, so every typed query (`.from(...).select(...)`) resolved its Row to `never` (e.g. `data.role` → "Property 'role' does not exist on type 'never'"). The direct `@supabase/supabase-js` client typed fine — only the ssr wrapper was broken. Upgrading to `@supabase/ssr@latest` (0.10.3) fixed it.

**How to apply:** keep `@supabase/ssr` current; if typed Supabase queries suddenly become `never`, check the ssr/supabase-js version pairing first. DB types are generated into `lib/supabase/database.types.ts` via `supabase gen types typescript --local`.

Mobile reflows perfectly: heading wraps, buttons stack full-width, cards become a single column — all within the 85% column. **Desktop-first + 85% (capped) verified at 375 / 1280 / 1440 / 2400px.**

input.content:
---
name: layout-desktop-first
description: Heard is desktop-first; the main section is 85% of viewport width, capped at 1500px
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Heard's layout is **desktop-first, then responsive down** — this overrides the design brief's "mobile-first" wording (the user corrected it after M0).

**Why:** the user wants the primary experience designed for desktop and the main content column to always read as a consistent proportion of the screen.

**How to apply:**
- The **main section spans 85% of the viewport width**, centred (7.5% gutters each side), **capped at 1500px** (`--container-app` in `app/globals.css` → `max-w-app`). Cap chosen so text lines stay readable for the low-vision audience on huge monitors.
- Use the shared **`components/shared/Container`** (`mx-auto w-[85%] max-w-app`) for the header inner, the page `<main>`, and the footer inner so they all align to the same column. Verified at 375/1280/1440/2400px.
- Write **desktop-first Tailwind**: base classes target desktop; use `max-md:` / `max-sm:` variants to adapt down (e.g. `grid-cols-3 max-md:grid-cols-1`, hero `text-display max-md:text-h1`, buttons `max-sm:w-full`). Don't default to mobile-first `sm:`/`md:` scaling-up.
- Focused forms (auth) still center a readable `max-w-md` card *inside* the 85% main.

Related: [[heard-build-plan]]

content.text:
Fixed and shipped. The auth pages are now genuinely desktop-first.

## ✅ Auth pages redesigned (desktop-first split)

Both `/signin` and `/signup` went from a small centered card to a **two-column split** that fills the 85% column:
- **Left**: a teal brand panel — white wordmark, "A calm place to talk, and to be heard.", a reassurance checklist, and the trust line.
- **Right**: the form (role selector, fields, submit).
- **Mobile**: stacks to a single column (panel on top, form below).

Verified live at 1440px (split) and 375px (stacked).

**Also fixed a real bug along the way:** my `globals.css` element defaults were unlayered, so `h1–h4 { color: ink }` was overriding Tailwind's `text-*` utilities — that's why the panel heading first rendered dark instead of white. I moved the defaults into `@layer base` and made headings inherit color, so any colored section (now and in future milestones) recolors its headings correctly. That's saved to memory so it won't recur.

`typecheck` ✓ · `lint` ✓ · 25/25 tests ✓.

**Shipped:** [PR #3](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/3) → merged to `main`.

A note for context: the earlier marketing/home change *was* live (you can hard-refresh to see it) — but you were right that the auth pages specifically were still mobile-style; those are the ones this PR fixes. From here, every screen I build follows the desktop-first + 85% convention by default.

input.content:
-- =====================================================================
-- Seed: 1 admin, 1 customer, 6 approved providers (from the prototype data).
-- All seeded accounts use the password: password123  (local dev only).
-- Inserting into auth.users fires handle_new_user(), which creates the
-- profile (+ a pending provider row for providers); we then fill in the
-- full provider data and mark them approved.
-- =====================================================================

-- Helper: create a confirmed email/password auth user with an identity so the
-- account can actually sign in locally. Returns nothing; the sign-up trigger
-- creates the matching profile/provider rows.
create or replace function public._seed_user(
  p_id uuid, p_email text, p_password text, p_role text, p_name text
) returns void
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  insert into auth.users (
    instance_id, id, aud, role, email, encrypted_password,
    email_confirmed_at, created_at, updated_at,
    raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data, is_sso_user, is_anonymous
  ) values (
    '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', p_id, 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
    p_email, crypt(p_password, gen_salt('bf')),
    now(), now(), now(),
    '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}'::jsonb,
    jsonb_build_object('role', p_role, 'full_name', p_name),
    false, false
  );

  insert into auth.identities (
    id, user_id, provider_id, provider, identity_data,
    last_sign_in_at, created_at, updated_at
  ) values (
    gen_random_uuid(), p_id, p_id::text, 'email',
    jsonb_build_object('sub', p_id::text, 'email', p_email, 'email_verified', true),
    now(), now(), now()
  );
end;
$$;
