-- Helper: create a confirmed email/password auth user with an identity so the
-- account can actually sign in locally. Returns nothing; the sign-up trigger
-- creates the matching profile/provider rows.
create or replace function public._seed_user(
  p_id uuid, p_email text, p_password text, p_role text, p_name text
) returns void
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  insert into auth.users (
    instance_id, id, aud, role, email, encrypted_password,
    email_confirmed_at, created_at, updated_at,
    raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data, is_sso_user, is_anonymous
  ) values (
    '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', p_id, 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
    p_email, crypt(p_password, gen_salt('bf')),
    now(), now(), now(),
    '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}'::jsonb,
    jsonb_build_object('role', p_role, 'full_name', p_name),
    false, false
  );

  insert into auth.identities (
    id, user_id, provider_id, provider, identity_data,
    last_sign_in_at, created_at, updated_at

    jsonb_build_object('sub', p_id::text, 'email', p_email, 'email_verified', true),
    now(), now(), now()
  );
end;
$$;

-- =====================================================================
-- Seed: 1 admin, 1 customer, 6 approved providers (from the prototype data).
-- All seeded accounts use the password: password123  (local dev only).
-- Inserting into auth.users fires handle_new_user(), which creates the
-- profile (+ a pending provider row for providers); we then fill in the

-- ---- Accounts -------------------------------------------------------
-- Set-based inserts (no function / dollar-quoting, which the seed runner's
-- statement batching mishandles). Inserting each auth.users row fires the
-- handle_new_user trigger → creates the profile (+ pending provider).
insert into auth.users (
  instance_id, id, aud, role, email, encrypted_password,
  email_confirmed_at, created_at, updated_at,
  raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data, is_sso_user, is_anonymous
)
select
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', u.id, 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
  u.email, crypt('password123', gen_salt('bf')),
  now(), now(), now(),
  '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}'::jsonb,
  jsonb_build_object('role', u.role, 'full_name', u.name),
  false, false
from (values
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1'::uuid, 'admin@heard.test',    'admin',    'Avery Admin'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1'::uuid, 'customer@heard.test', 'customer', 'Casey Customer'),

-- =====================================================================
-- Seed: 1 admin, 1 customer, 6 approved providers (from the prototype data).
-- All seeded accounts use the password: password123  (local dev only).
-- Inserting into auth.users fires handle_new_user(), which creates the
-- profile (+ a pending provider row for providers); we then fill in the
-- full provider data and mark them approved.
-- =====================================================================

-- ---- Accounts -------------------------------------------------------
-- Set-based inserts (no function / dollar-quoting, which the seed runner's
-- statement batching mishandles). Inserting each auth.users row fires the
-- handle_new_user trigger → creates the profile (+ pending provider).
insert into auth.users (
  instance_id, id, aud, role, email, encrypted_password,
  email_confirmed_at, created_at, updated_at,
  raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data, is_sso_user, is_anonymous
)
select
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', u.id, 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
  u.email, crypt('password123', gen_salt('bf')),
  now(), now(), now(),
  '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}'::jsonb,
  jsonb_build_object('role', u.role, 'full_name', u.name),
  false, false
from (values
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1'::uuid, 'admin@heard.test',    'admin',    'Avery Admin'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1'::uuid, 'customer@heard.test', 'customer', 'Casey Customer'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'::uuid, 'maya@heard.test',     'provider', 'Maya Lin'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002'::uuid, 'theo@heard.test',     'provider', 'Theo Park'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000003'::uuid, 'ines@heard.test',     'provider', 'Inés Romero'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000004'::uuid, 'walter@heard.test',   'provider', 'Walter Boyd'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000005'::uuid, 'priya@heard.test',    'provider', 'Priya Nair'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000006'::uuid, 'omar@heard.test',     'provider', 'Omar Haddad')
) as u(id, email, role, name);

-- Email identities so the seeded accounts can sign in locally.
insert into auth.identities (
  id, user_id, provider_id, provider, identity_data,
  last_sign_in_at, created_at, updated_at
)
select
  gen_random_uuid(), u.id, u.id::text, 'email',
  jsonb_build_object('sub', u.id::text, 'email', u.email, 'email_verified', true),
  now(), now(), now()
from (values
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000a1'::uuid, 'admin@heard.test'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000c1'::uuid, 'customer@heard.test'),
  ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'::uuid, 'maya@heard.test'),

content.text:
**M2 — integration adapters (mock) + pricing.** This is the layer that lets the whole app run end-to-end without Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, swappable for real later. Per SPEC §3.2 and the build plan:

**1. Three adapters**, each as `interface.ts` + `mock.ts` + `real.ts` (stubbed `// TODO`) + `index.ts` (picks by `INTEGRATIONS_MODE`):
- **Payments** (→ Stripe Connect later): `authorizeHold`, `capture`, `refund`, `recordProviderEarning`, `runWeeklyPayouts`, etc. Mock writes an in-DB ledger (`payments`/`payouts`) with synthetic `mock_pay_…` refs.
- **Calls** (→ Zoom Meeting SDK): `createSession`, `getJoinInfo`, `endSession`. Mock returns synthetic refs; the UI renders the in-app mock call screen (M6).
- **Background check** (→ Checkr): `initiate` → `pending`, `getStatus`. Mock returns `pending`; admin clears it (M4).

**2. `lib/pricing.ts`** — the single source of pricing truth, pure and fully unit-tested: `priceForBlock`, overage (`ceil` past the block), 5% commission from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`, tips (no commission), **half-up rounding**, all in integer cents.

**The rule it enforces:** feature code only ever calls `getPayments()/getCalls()/getBackgroundCheck()` — never imports `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, never touches an external SDK outside `real.ts`.

**Done when:** unit tests cover every mock adapter and all pricing cases; `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` still compiles (reaching the TODO stubs). No UI in this milestone — it's the plumbing M3–M7 build on.

It'll ship as `m2-adapters-pricing` → PR #5 → merge, same as the others.

**Heard** is a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind/visually impaired — non-clinical companionship, never therapy. Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body) and provider dignity are the whole point. Stack: Next.js 16 App Router + TS strict + Supabase + Tailwind v4 + Zod + Vitest/RTL/jest-axe + Playwright. External services (payments/calls/background-check) are mocked behind adapters (`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`); money is integer cents; all pricing in `lib/pricing.ts`; all copy via `messages/en.json`.

Governing docs live at repo root: `SPEC.md`, `BUILD_PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Design tokens are in `app/globals.css` (@theme), ported from the design system.

**Working agreement:** build milestone-by-milestone (M0→M9) with a **checkpoint** after each — stop, show it runs, get sign-off before the next.

**Progress:**
- **M0 (done, committed `4066c54` on main):** scaffold, design tokens, accessible UI primitives, i18n, email+password auth with customer/provider role selection (role persisted via a Postgres `handle_new_user` trigger that also creates a `providers` row status=pending), RLS on profiles/providers, SSR clients + `proxy.ts` (Next 16 renamed middleware→proxy) route guards, app shell + persistent crisis-safety affordance. 25 tests green.

**Heard** is a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind/visually impaired — non-clinical companionship, never therapy. Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body) and provider dignity are the whole point. Stack: Next.js 16 App Router + TS strict + Supabase + Tailwind v4 + Zod + Vitest/RTL/jest-axe + Playwright. External services (payments/calls/background-check) are mocked behind adapters (`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`); money is integer cents; all pricing in `lib/pricing.ts`; all copy via `messages/en.json`.

Governing docs live at repo root: `SPEC.md`, `BUILD_PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Design tokens are in `app/globals.css` (@theme), ported from the design system.

**Working agreement:** build milestone-by-milestone (M0→M9) with a **checkpoint** after each — stop, show it runs, get sign-off before the next.

**Progress:**
- **M0 (done, committed `4066c54` on main):** scaffold, design tokens, accessible UI primitives, i18n, email+password auth with customer/provider role selection (role persisted via a Postgres `handle_new_user` trigger that also creates a `providers` row status=pending), RLS on profiles/providers, SSR clients + `proxy.ts` (Next 16 renamed middleware→proxy) route guards, app shell + persistent crisis-safety affordance. 25 tests green.
- **M1 (done, PR #4):** full data model for all SPEC §4 tables + RLS on every table; `seed.sql` (admin + customer + 6 approved providers, all sign in with `password123`); `lib/db/queries.ts` (RLS-enforced reads, public provider reads omit bg_check_ref/payout_account_ref) + entity Zod schemas. `supabase db reset` clean; RLS verified. Seed gotcha: insert `auth.users` set-based with empty-string token columns (confirmation_token etc.) or GoTrue 500s on login; add an `auth.identities` row so accounts can sign in; no dollar-quoted functions in seed.sql (the runner's batcher breaks them).
- **M2 (done, PR #5):** integration adapters under `lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/{interface,mock,real,index}.ts` — call `getPayments()/getCalls()/getBackgroundCheck()`, never import mock/real directly; real stubs throw `// TODO` errors. `lib/pricing.ts` is the only place for money math (pure, integer cents, half-up commission from config). Payments mock takes an injected Supabase client (no server-only) so it's unit-testable. 66 tests.
- **M3 (next):** provider side — `/provider/onboarding` (audio-first: record/upload voice intro to Storage, topics/languages, block prices, availability, `backgroundCheck.initiate()` → pending) and `/provider/dashboard` (Available-now toggle, sessions, weekly earnings, rating). Keyboard/SR-verified; axe passes. This is the accessibility showcase flow.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

content.text:
**Next is M6 — Session lifecycle.** This is where a confirmed booking turns into an actual (mock) conversation and gets billed. It's the piece that connects everything you've built so far.

**The flow:**
- **`/session/[id]`** — customer side. Pre-call waiting room ("Connecting you with Maya…", mic-check, cancel) → in-call **mock screen**: large avatar + audio waveform, the listener's name, a **count-up timer**, and a control bar (Mute · Captions toggle · End).
- **`/provider/session/[id]`** — provider side mirrors it: incoming request → Accept → in-session, plus a discreet **"Report / End for safety"** control.
- **On End:** read the elapsed time from the timer → `computeSessionAccounting` (block + overage + 5% commission + provider earnings) → `payments.capture(total)` → write the `session` row (`completed`) → route to the summary.

**Wiring it uses what's already in place:** the `calls` adapter (`getCalls()` → `createSession`/`getJoinInfo`/`endSession`, all mock), `lib/pricing.ts` for the final accounting, and `payments.capture` against the hold from M5.

**Done when:** a full mock call runs, the timer drives elapsed time, and the final accounting is **correct and persisted** — verified by the pricing-path unit tests.

It'll ship as `m6-session-lifecycle` → PR #9 → merge, same as the rest.

One small heads-up: the count-up timer and mute/captions toggles are genuinely interactive client state, and "End" needs to compute from the live elapsed seconds — so I'll be careful that the timer is the source of truth (as the brief specifies for mock mode).

# Heard

A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with — and be listened to by —
professional companion listeners, all of whom are legally blind or visually
impaired. **Companionship and conversation, not therapy.** Accessibility is the
product, not a layer.

See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for the full build spec, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
the conventions every change follows, and [`BUILD_PLAN.md`](BUILD_PLAN.md) for
the milestones.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth +
Storage) · Tailwind v4 · Zod · Vitest + Testing Library + `jest-axe` ·
Playwright. External services (payments, calls, background checks) are reached
only through adapters and run in **mock** mode by default.

## Prerequisites

- Node 20+ and npm.
- A local container runtime + the Supabase CLI. On macOS without Docker Desktop,
  a headless setup works:

  ```sh
  brew install supabase/tap/supabase colima docker
  colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
  ```

  Colima exposes its Docker socket at `~/.colima/default/docker.sock`. If the
  Supabase/Docker CLIs can't find it, export:

  ```sh
  export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"
  ```

## Setup

```sh
npm install
supabase start                 # applies migrations in supabase/migrations/
supabase db reset              # apply migrations + seed (6 providers, admin, customer)
supabase status -o env         # copy the keys below into .env.local
```

Create `.env.local` (see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) using the values from
`supabase status`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<ANON_KEY>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<SERVICE_ROLE_KEY>
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
```

Then:

```sh
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

### Try it — seeded accounts

All seeded accounts use the password **`password123`**:

| Role     | Email                  | What you can do                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Customer | `customer@heard.test`  | Browse, book, run a mock call, rate + tip        |
| Listener | `maya@heard.test`      | Dashboard, availability, sessions, earnings      |
| Admin    | `admin@heard.test`     | Approve/reject/suspend listeners, run payouts    |

(There are 6 seeded listeners: maya, theo, ines, walter, priya, omar.)

> Local notes:
> - `supabase/config.toml` disables the `analytics` (Vector) container — it
>   bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's virtiofs mount doesn't support.
> - `next.config.ts` sets `allowedDevOrigins` so server actions work when the dev
>   server is driven from `127.0.0.1` (Playwright).

## Scripts

```sh
npm run dev          # local dev
npm run build        # production build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
npm run test         # vitest (unit + component, incl. axe a11y checks)
npm run test:e2e     # playwright (needs local Supabase + dev server)
npm run db:reset     # supabase db reset (re-applies migrations + seed)
```

### End-to-end tests

The two Playwright happy paths (`tests/e2e/`) drive the real app, so they need a
running local Supabase with a fresh seed:

```sh
supabase db reset
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm run test:e2e
```

They cover: (a) customer browse → book → mock session → rate; (b) provider
onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.

## Database types

`lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is generated from the live schema. Regenerate
after any migration:

```sh
supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public > lib/supabase/database.types.ts
```

## Swapping a mock adapter for a real one

Every external service is behind an adapter in
`lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/`, each with
`interface.ts` · `mock.ts` · `real.ts` · `index.ts`. Feature code only ever
calls `getPayments()` / `getCalls()` / `getBackgroundCheck()` from `index.ts` —
it never imports `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and the external SDKs are only
imported inside `real.ts`.

To go live with one (e.g. payments):

1. Implement the methods in `lib/integrations/payments/real.ts` against the SDK
   (the `// TODO` stubs mark each one). Keep the same `interface.ts` contract.
2. Add the provider's keys to your environment (see the commented block in
   [`.env.example`](.env.example)).
3. Set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`. `index.ts` then returns the real adapter;
   nothing else in the app changes.

Mappings: **payments → Stripe Connect** (Express accounts host funds + payouts),
**calls → Zoom Meeting SDK** (platform-owned host pool + S2S OAuth + webhook
metering), **background-check → Checkr**. The build already compiles in
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`; calling a method just reaches its `// TODO` stub until
implemented.

## Project shape

```
app/                 route groups: (marketing) (auth) (customer) (provider) (admin)
components/          ui/ (design-system primitives) + customer/ provider/ admin/ session/ shared/
lib/                 integrations/  supabase/  db/queries.ts  validation/schemas.ts  pricing.ts  auth.ts
messages/en.json     all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
supabase/            migrations/  seed.sql  config.toml
tests/               unit/  component/  e2e/
```

## Status

**Build complete (M0–M9).** All routes implemented; both E2E happy paths pass;
integrations run in mock mode end-to-end with a seeded set of 6 providers, and
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to the clearly-marked `// TODO` stubs. All
money flows through `lib/pricing.ts` (integer cents, commission from config);
RLS is enforced on every table; accessibility is axe-checked across components.
Fast-follows (real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, a moderation UI, native mobile,
subscriptions) are intentionally out of scope — the schema and adapters are
ready for them.
```

# Heard

A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with — and be listened to by —
professional companion listeners, all of whom are legally blind or visually
impaired. **Companionship and conversation, not therapy.** Accessibility is the
product, not a layer.

See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for the full build spec, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
the conventions every change follows, and [`BUILD_PLAN.md`](BUILD_PLAN.md) for
the milestones.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth +
Storage) · Tailwind v4 · Zod · Vitest + Testing Library + `jest-axe` ·
Playwright. External services (payments, calls, background checks) are reached
only through adapters and run in **mock** mode by default.

## Prerequisites

- Node 20+ and npm.
- A local container runtime + the Supabase CLI. On macOS without Docker Desktop,
  a headless setup works:

  ```sh
  brew install supabase/tap/supabase colima docker
  colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
  ```

  Colima exposes its Docker socket at `~/.colima/default/docker.sock`. If the
  Supabase/Docker CLIs can't find it, export:

  ```sh
  export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"
  ```

## Setup

```sh
npm install
supabase start                 # applies migrations in supabase/migrations/
supabase db reset              # apply migrations + seed (6 providers, admin, customer)
supabase status -o env         # copy the keys below into .env.local
```

Create `.env.local` (see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) using the values from
`supabase status`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<ANON_KEY>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<SERVICE_ROLE_KEY>
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
```

Then:

```sh
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

### Try it — seeded accounts

All seeded accounts use the password **`password123`**:

| Role     | Email                  | What you can do                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Customer | `customer@heard.test`  | Browse, book, run a mock call, rate + tip        |
| Listener | `maya@heard.test`      | Dashboard, availability, sessions, earnings      |
| Admin    | `admin@heard.test`     | Approve/reject/suspend listeners, run payouts    |

(There are 6 seeded listeners: maya, theo, ines, walter, priya, omar.)

> Local notes:
> - `supabase/config.toml` disables the `analytics` (Vector) container — it
>   bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's virtiofs mount doesn't support.
> - `next.config.ts` sets `allowedDevOrigins` so server actions work when the dev
>   server is driven from `127.0.0.1` (Playwright).

## Scripts

```sh
npm run dev          # local dev
npm run build        # production build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
npm run test         # vitest (unit + component, incl. axe a11y checks)
npm run test:e2e     # playwright (needs local Supabase + dev server)
npm run db:reset     # supabase db reset (re-applies migrations + seed)
```

### End-to-end tests

The two Playwright happy paths (`tests/e2e/`) drive the real app, so they need a
running local Supabase with a fresh seed:

```sh
supabase db reset
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm run test:e2e
```

They cover: (a) customer browse → book → mock session → rate; (b) provider
onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.

## Database types

`lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is generated from the live schema. Regenerate
after any migration:

```sh
supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public > lib/supabase/database.types.ts
```

## Swapping a mock adapter for a real one

Every external service is behind an adapter in
`lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/`, each with
`interface.ts` · `mock.ts` · `real.ts` · `index.ts`. Feature code only ever
calls `getPayments()` / `getCalls()` / `getBackgroundCheck()` from `index.ts` —
it never imports `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and the external SDKs are only
imported inside `real.ts`.

To go live with one (e.g. payments):

1. Implement the methods in `lib/integrations/payments/real.ts` against the SDK
   (the `// TODO` stubs mark each one). Keep the same `interface.ts` contract.
2. Add the provider's keys to your environment (see the commented block in
   [`.env.example`](.env.example)).
3. Set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`. `index.ts` then returns the real adapter;
   nothing else in the app changes.

Mappings: **payments → Stripe Connect** (Express accounts host funds + payouts),
**calls → Zoom Meeting SDK** (platform-owned host pool + S2S OAuth + webhook
metering), **background-check → Checkr**. The build already compiles in
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`; calling a method just reaches its `// TODO` stub until
implemented.

## Project shape

```
app/                 route groups: (marketing) (auth) (customer) (provider) (admin)
components/          ui/ (design-system primitives) + customer/ provider/ admin/ session/ shared/
lib/                 integrations/  supabase/  db/queries.ts  validation/schemas.ts  pricing.ts  auth.ts
messages/en.json     all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
supabase/            migrations/  seed.sql  config.toml
tests/               unit/  component/  e2e/
```

## Status

**Build complete (M0–M9).** All routes implemented; both E2E happy paths pass;
integrations run in mock mode end-to-end with a seeded set of 6 providers, and
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to the clearly-marked `// TODO` stubs. All
money flows through `lib/pricing.ts` (integer cents, commission from config);
RLS is enforced on every table; accessibility is axe-checked across components.
Fast-follows (real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, a moderation UI, native mobile,
subscriptions) are intentionally out of scope — the schema and adapters are
ready for them.
```

**Heard** is a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind/visually impaired — non-clinical companionship, never therapy. Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body) and provider dignity are the whole point. Stack: Next.js 16 App Router + TS strict + Supabase + Tailwind v4 + Zod + Vitest/RTL/jest-axe + Playwright. External services (payments/calls/background-check) are mocked behind adapters (`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`); money is integer cents; all pricing in `lib/pricing.ts`; all copy via `messages/en.json`.

Governing docs live at repo root: `SPEC.md`, `BUILD_PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Design tokens are in `app/globals.css` (@theme), ported from the design system.

**Working agreement:** build milestone-by-milestone (M0→M9) with a **checkpoint** after each — stop, show it runs, get sign-off before the next.

**Progress:**
- **M0 (done, committed `4066c54` on main):** scaffold, design tokens, accessible UI primitives, i18n, email+password auth with customer/provider role selection (role persisted via a Postgres `handle_new_user` trigger that also creates a `providers` row status=pending), RLS on profiles/providers, SSR clients + `proxy.ts` (Next 16 renamed middleware→proxy) route guards, app shell + persistent crisis-safety affordance. 25 tests green.
- **M1 (done, PR #4):** full data model for all SPEC §4 tables + RLS on every table; `seed.sql` (admin + customer + 6 approved providers, all sign in with `password123`); `lib/db/queries.ts` (RLS-enforced reads, public provider reads omit bg_check_ref/payout_account_ref) + entity Zod schemas. `supabase db reset` clean; RLS verified. Seed gotcha: insert `auth.users` set-based with empty-string token columns (confirmation_token etc.) or GoTrue 500s on login; add an `auth.identities` row so accounts can sign in; no dollar-quoted functions in seed.sql (the runner's batcher breaks them).

- **M7 (then):** `/session/[id]/summary` rating + optional tip + receipt (recompute rating, addTip); weekly mock payouts (runWeeklyPayouts) + payout history. **M8:** full a11y/visual polish pass + report hook. **M9:** E2E (2 happy paths), README, verify INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real compiles.

# 🎉 The Heard build is complete — all of M0–M9 shipped.

Every milestone is built, verified end-to-end, and merged to `main` as its own PR (#1–#12) in the repo [github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard).

## This session (M6 → M9)
| Milestone | What landed | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| **M6 — Session lifecycle** ([#9](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/9)) | Pre-call → mock call (count-up timer, mute, captions, end), provider mirror; end → pricing → capture | $24 total / $1.20 commission / $22.80 earnings, payment **captured** |
| **M7 — Reviews, tips, payouts** ([#10](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/10)) | Rating + optional tip (no commission), rating recompute, admin weekly payouts | Maya 5.00★, **$22.80 payout** on her dashboard |
| **M8 — A11y + report hook** ([#11](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/11)) | "Report a problem" → `reports` table, live-region announcements, safety on every page | Report row written (reporter-scoped) |
| **M9 — Tests, docs, handoff** ([#12](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/12)) | 2 Playwright E2E paths, full README, real-mode build | **Both E2E pass**; `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` builds all 16 routes |

## The whole app now works end-to-end (mock mode)
Provider onboards (audio-first) → admin approves → customer discovers by voice & books → mock call runs & bills correctly → customer rates/tips → weekly payout. All money flows through `lib/pricing.ts` (integer cents, 5% from config); RLS on every table; accessibility axe-checked throughout; desktop-first 85% layout.

**Final state:** `typecheck` ✓ · `lint` ✓ · **87 unit/component tests** ✓ · **2 E2E happy paths** ✓ · real-mode build ✓.

One gotcha worth remembering (saved to memory): Next 16 silently blocks cross-origin server actions, so `allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1","localhost"]` in `next.config.ts` was needed for the Playwright-driven flows.

Per the brief, the deliberate fast-follows remain out of scope — real **Stripe Connect / Zoom Meeting SDK / Checkr** (the README documents exactly how to swap each mock for the real adapter), a moderation UI on the `reports` table, native mobile, and subscriptions. The schema and adapter seams are all in place for them.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

## n8n
This is the official MCP server for n8n, a workflow automation platform.

This MCP server provides tools to build n8n workflows programmatically using the n8n Workflow SDK.

To build n8n workflows, follow these steps in order:

1. Read the SDK reference: You MUST call get_sdk_reference (or use the n8n://workflow-sdk/reference resource) before writing workflow code. Do not guess SDK syntax.

2. Get suggested nodes: You MUST call get_suggested_nodes with all relevant workflow technique categories before searching for nodes. Use the recommendations, pattern hints, and configuration guidance to decide which nodes and patterns to use.

3. Discover nodes: Call search_nodes with queries for services you need (e.g., ["gmail", "slack", "schedule trigger"]), utility nodes (e.g., ["set", "if", "merge", "code"]), and suggested nodes you plan to use. Note the discriminators (resource/operation/mode) in the results.

4. Get type definitions: Call get_node_types with ALL node IDs you plan to use, including discriminators from search results. This returns the exact TypeScript parameter definitions. DO NOT skip this — guessing parameter names creates invalid workflows.

5. Write the workflow code using the SDK patterns from the reference and the exact parameter names from the type definitions. Follow the coding guidelines and design guidance sections of the SDK reference (retrieve them with get_sdk_reference using sections "guidelines" and "design").

6. Validate: Call validate_workflow with your full code. Fix any errors and re-validate until valid.

7. Create: Call create_workflow_from_code with the validated code to save the workflow to n8n. Include a short `description` (1-2 sentences) summarizing what the workflow does — this helps users find and understand their workflows.

# Dashboards Build Plan — "Heard" (M10–M14)

Continues `BUILD_PLAN.md` after the M0–M9 MVP. Builds the fuller **Listener / Customer / Admin** dashboards per `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md`. Runs fully in **mock mode** — no new integrations. All the rules in `CLAUDE.md` still apply (accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA, adapter pattern, money in integer cents via `lib/pricing.ts`, RLS on every table).

**Kickoff prompt for Claude Code:**
> Read `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, then implement `DASHBOARDS_BUILD_PLAN.md` starting at **M10**, **one milestone at a time**. At the end of each: run typecheck, lint, tests, and an **axe pass on every dashboard screen**; show me how to verify it; wait for my go-ahead. Reuse the existing `components/ui`, schema, and `lib/pricing.ts`. Money stays in cents; add RLS to new tables; read admin metrics from SQL views, don't compute them in the UI.

Legend: each milestone has **Tasks** and **Done when** (acceptance criteria).

---

## M10 — Dashboard foundation (shared)
**Tasks**
- [ ] Migration: `favorites` (customer_id, provider_id) + RLS (owner-scoped); update `seed.sql`.
- [ ] Migration: `notifications` (user_id, type, payload, read_at) + RLS *(optional; powers activity feeds)*.
- [ ] Migration: SQL views `admin_metrics_strategic`, `admin_metrics_operational`, `admin_metrics_alerts` (all money in cents).
- [ ] Shared dashboard shell: role-aware layout + nav, landmarks/regions, and the persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" link.
- [ ] Accessible primitives in `components/ui`: `StatCard` (labeled number), `DataTable` (semantic `<table>` with `<th scope>`, `<thead>`, caption; keyboard-operable sort that announces state), `StatusBadge` (text + icon, never color-only).
- [ ] Unit tests for the metric views/queries; axe tests for the primitives.

**Done when:** `supabase db reset` applies the new tables + views with seed data; primitives pass axe; RLS verified (a user cannot read another user's favorites/notifications).

---

## M11 — Listener (provider) dashboard  *[priority — accessibility-first]*
**Tasks**
- [ ] Availability section: reuse the MVP toggle (announce "You're available / offline" via live region) + next scheduled session.
- [ ] At-a-glance `StatCard`s: this week's earnings, pending/uncleared, next payout date, average rating, sessions this week.
- [ ] Incoming requests (Accept / Decline) + upcoming confirmed sessions (time, customer first name, block length).
- [ ] Recent sessions `DataTable`: date, duration, block + overage, earnings, rating.
- [ ] Earnings & payouts: balance, this month, lifetime; payout history table (period, amount, status).
- [ ] Feedback: recent reviews (rating, comment, tip).
- [ ] Profile-health checklist (voice intro, topics, languages, prices, availability; approval / background-check status) with edit links.

**Done when:** a seeded provider sees accurate earnings/sessions/feedback; a **keyboard-only + screen-reader walkthrough succeeds**; axe passes. Data maps to `providers`, `sessions`, `payouts`, `bookings`, `reviews` (no new tables).

---

## M12 — Customer (client) dashboard
**Tasks**
- [ ] Resume / quick-start: "Talk now" + a next-upcoming-session banner.
- [ ] Favorite listeners (uses `favorites`): list with voice-intro play + "Talk now / Rebook"; add/remove favorite from the profile and browse screens.
- [ ] Upcoming bookings with reschedule / cancel (respect the cancel policy in `SPEC.md` §5).
- [ ] Past sessions `DataTable`: date, listener, duration, amount, "Rebook" / leave-or-see review.
- [ ] Receipts / contributions: payment history with a downloadable receipt (label via `messages/en.json` so fee-vs-donation wording can switch).
- [ ] Payment & settings (method, notifications, language, profile); always-visible Help + safety link.

**Done when:** a seeded customer can favorite a listener, rebook, reschedule/cancel, and view receipts; axe + keyboard pass on every screen.

---

## M13 — Admin dashboard
**Tasks**
- [ ] Fold the existing approvals queue into the dashboard shell.
- [ ] Strategic + alert `StatCard`s from `admin_metrics_*` views: GMV (session value), platform revenue, active providers, active customers, approval backlog, open reports, churn, cancellations, failed payments.
- [ ] Operational metrics: booking→session conversion, provider activation, completion rate, supply/demand balance.
- [ ] **Reports & safety review UI**: inbox of `reports` → review, contact, suspend (pulled forward from `SPEC.md` §12 — the safety backbone for protecting blind providers).
- [ ] Basic user management: search, view detail, suspend / reinstate.
- [ ] Read-only sessions and payments/payouts views.
- [ ] Config panel: display commission rate (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`); editing is later.

**Done when:** admin sees live metrics from the views, can action a report and suspend a user, and the approval flow still works; non-admins are blocked (RLS + route guard); any chart has a table + text-summary fallback; axe passes.

---

## M14 — Accessibility, tests, polish
**Tasks**
- [ ] Full pass against `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md` §4 on all three dashboards: semantic tables, no color-only status, visible focus, live-region announcements, reduced density.
- [ ] Component tests + axe for each dashboard; extend Playwright: (a) provider views earnings; (b) customer favorites → rebook; (c) admin actions a report.
- [ ] Warm/consistent styling; empty / loading / error states; quick performance check on the metric views.

**Done when:** every dashboard screen passes axe and a keyboard-only walkthrough; the new E2E paths and CI are green.

---

**Notes**
- Continues the M-numbering — append these to `BUILD_PLAN.md` or keep this file alongside it.
- Mock mode only; no Stripe/Zoom/Checkr work here.
- Build order is deliberate: foundation → listener (highest stakes for accessibility) → customer → admin → hardening.

1	# Dashboards — Requirements ("Heard")
2	
3	What the three role dashboards need: **Listener** (provider), **Customer** (client), and **Admin**. This is the research-and-requirements step *before* building. It maps to the existing data model in `SPEC.md` §4 and the warm/accessible design in `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Hand this to Claude Code as the spec for a "Dashboards" milestone.
4	
5	> The M0–M9 MVP already ships *basic* versions of each (provider availability + earnings, admin approval queue, customer account/history). This document defines the **fuller dashboards** and marks what to add **now** vs **later**.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. Cross-cutting principles
10	
11	**Build on what exists.** Reuse the `components/ui` primitives, the schema, and `lib/pricing.ts`. Metrics are computed by queries/SQL views — see §5; only two small new tables are needed (favorites, notifications).
12	
13	**Accessibility for dashboards is the hard part — especially the Listener view, whose users are blind.** From the research, apply these as rules:
14	- Prefer **labeled "stat cards" (plain numbers) and semantic data tables** over charts. If a chart is used, it must be paired with an equivalent **data table** and a one-line **text summary of the takeaway**.
15	- Tables use real `<table>` semantics: `<th scope=…>`, `<thead>`, captions. Screen readers must announce headers.
16	- **Never encode meaning in color alone** — add text/icon/pattern. Contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
17	- Everything keyboard-operable, logical tab order, visible focus; state changes announced via live regions (e.g., "You're now available").
18	- **Reduce density.** Use filters and progressive disclosure; don't crowd the screen. This helps everyone and is essential for screen-reader users.
19	
20	**Money & framing.** All amounts in integer cents via `lib/pricing.ts`. Labels adapt to the eventual model: "Earnings" (listener), "Receipts/Contributions" (customer) — keep copy in `messages/en.json` so the fee-vs-donation wording can switch.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. Listener (provider) dashboard — *the priority*
25	
26	**Purpose:** one calm place to go available, see who's coming, track earnings, and keep their profile healthy. Must be flawless by screen reader.
27	
28	### Sections / widgets
29	| Section | Shows | Notes |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| **Availability** | Big **"Available now"** toggle with text state ("You're available" / "You're offline"); next scheduled session | Already in MVP. Toggle announces state via live region. |
32	| **At a glance (stat cards)** | This week's earnings · pending (uncleared) · next payout date · average rating · sessions this week | Plain labeled numbers, not charts. |
33	| **Incoming & upcoming** | Pending requests (Accept / Decline) + upcoming confirmed sessions (time, customer first name, block length) | Accept/Decline are large, clearly labeled. |
34	| **Recent sessions** | Table: date, duration, block + overage, earnings, rating left | Semantic table; sortable optional. |
35	| **Earnings & payouts** | Balance, this month, lifetime; payout history (date, period, amount, status) | Maps to `sessions` + `payouts`. |
36	| **Feedback** | Recent reviews (rating + comment + tip) | From `reviews`. |
37	| **Profile health** | Completeness checklist: voice intro ✓, topics, languages, prices, availability; **approval / background-check status** | Drives activation; links to edit. |
38	| **Simple performance** *(later)* | Profile views, voice-intro plays, bookings, conversion (last 7 days) | Keep minimal; numbers + table, no dense viz. |
39	
40	### Key actions
41	Go available/offline · accept/decline a request · join a session · edit profile/voice intro/prices/availability · view payout detail · respond to a review.
42	
43	### Data (existing tables)
44	`providers` (status, rating, prices, availability), `sessions` (earnings, durations, counts), `payouts`, `bookings` (incoming/upcoming), `reviews`. No new tables required.
45	
46	### MVP-now vs later
47	- **Now:** availability, at-a-glance stat cards, incoming/upcoming, recent sessions table, earnings + payout history, feedback, profile-health checklist.
48	- **Later:** performance analytics (views/plays/conversion), messaging, goal-setting.
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 2. Customer (client) dashboard
53	
54	**Purpose:** get back into a conversation fast, manage bookings, and find receipts — low-pressure, warm, reassuring.
55	
56	### Sections / widgets
57	| Section | Shows | Notes |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| **Resume / quick start** | "Talk now" entry + **next upcoming session** ("Next session: Tue 7:00pm with Maria") | Most-common need at the top. |
60	| **Favorite listeners** | Saved listeners with voice-intro play + **"Talk now / Rebook"** | Needs a small new `favorites` table (§5). |
61	| **Upcoming bookings** | Time, listener, block length, with **reschedule / cancel** | From `bookings`; respect the cancel policy in `SPEC.md` §5. |
62	| **Past sessions** | Table: date, listener, duration, amount, "Rebook" · "Leave/See review" | From `sessions` + `reviews`. |
63	| **Receipts / contributions** | Payment history with downloadable receipts | Label adapts to fee vs donation model. |
64	| **Payment & settings** | Manage payment method, notifications, language, profile | From `profiles` + payment adapter. |
65	| **Help & safety** | Always-visible Help; the persistent **"companionship, not therapy / crisis support"** link | Required on every screen. |
66	
67	### Key actions
68	Talk now / rebook · favorite a listener · reschedule or cancel · leave a rating + tip · download a receipt · update payment/settings.
69	
70	### Data
71	`bookings`, `sessions`, `payments`, `reviews`, `profiles`, **+ new `favorites`**.
72	
73	### MVP-now vs later
74	- **Now:** resume/next session, upcoming + past bookings, receipts, payment/settings, help/safety.
75	- **Later:** favorites (small schema add — could be now if quick), spending summary, notification preferences detail.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 3. Admin dashboard
80	
81	**Purpose:** run the marketplace safely — approve supply, watch health, act on problems. The MVP shipped "provider approval only"; this expands it.
82	
83	### Layout — three KPI tiers (from marketplace research)
84	| Tier | Cadence | Metrics for "Heard" |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| **Strategic** | Monthly | Total session value (GMV) · platform revenue (commission) · active providers · active customers · avg rating / NPS |
87	| **Operational** | Weekly | Booking→session conversion · **provider activation** (approved → first session) · session completion rate · supply/demand balance (available listeners vs requests) |
88	| **Alert** | Real-time / daily | **Approval backlog** · open reports/disputes · provider churn · cancellation/no-show rate · failed payments |
89	
90	### Operational tools (sections)
91	| Section | Function | Status |
92	|---|---|---|

# Dashboards — Requirements ("Heard")

What the three role dashboards need: **Listener** (provider), **Customer** (client), and **Admin**. This is the research-and-requirements step *before* building. It maps to the existing data model in `SPEC.md` §4 and the warm/accessible design in `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Hand this to Claude Code as the spec for a "Dashboards" milestone.

> The M0–M9 MVP already ships *basic* versions of each (provider availability + earnings, admin approval queue, customer account/history). This document defines the **fuller dashboards** and marks what to add **now** vs **later**.

---

## 0. Cross-cutting principles

**Build on what exists.** Reuse the `components/ui` primitives, the schema, and `lib/pricing.ts`. Metrics are computed by queries/SQL views — see §5; only two small new tables are needed (favorites, notifications).

**Accessibility for dashboards is the hard part — especially the Listener view, whose users are blind.** From the research, apply these as rules:
- Prefer **labeled "stat cards" (plain numbers) and semantic data tables** over charts. If a chart is used, it must be paired with an equivalent **data table** and a one-line **text summary of the takeaway**.
- Tables use real `<table>` semantics: `<th scope=…>`, `<thead>`, captions. Screen readers must announce headers.
- **Never encode meaning in color alone** — add text/icon/pattern. Contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
- Everything keyboard-operable, logical tab order, visible focus; state changes announced via live regions (e.g., "You're now available").
- **Reduce density.** Use filters and progressive disclosure; don't crowd the screen. This helps everyone and is essential for screen-reader users.

**Money & framing.** All amounts in integer cents via `lib/pricing.ts`. Labels adapt to the eventual model: "Earnings" (listener), "Receipts/Contributions" (customer) — keep copy in `messages/en.json` so the fee-vs-donation wording can switch.

---

## 1. Listener (provider) dashboard — *the priority*

**Purpose:** one calm place to go available, see who's coming, track earnings, and keep their profile healthy. Must be flawless by screen reader.

### Sections / widgets
| Section | Shows | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Availability** | Big **"Available now"** toggle with text state ("You're available" / "You're offline"); next scheduled session | Already in MVP. Toggle announces state via live region. |
| **At a glance (stat cards)** | This week's earnings · pending (uncleared) · next payout date · average rating · sessions this week | Plain labeled numbers, not charts. |
| **Incoming & upcoming** | Pending requests (Accept / Decline) + upcoming confirmed sessions (time, customer first name, block length) | Accept/Decline are large, clearly labeled. |
| **Recent sessions** | Table: date, duration, block + overage, earnings, rating left | Semantic table; sortable optional. |
| **Earnings & payouts** | Balance, this month, lifetime; payout history (date, period, amount, status) | Maps to `sessions` + `payouts`. |
| **Feedback** | Recent reviews (rating + comment + tip) | From `reviews`. |
| **Profile health** | Completeness checklist: voice intro ✓, topics, languages, prices, availability; **approval / background-check status** | Drives activation; links to edit. |
| **Simple performance** *(later)* | Profile views, voice-intro plays, bookings, conversion (last 7 days) | Keep minimal; numbers + table, no dense viz. |

### Key actions
Go available/offline · accept/decline a request · join a session · edit profile/voice intro/prices/availability · view payout detail · respond to a review.

### Data (existing tables)
`providers` (status, rating, prices, availability), `sessions` (earnings, durations, counts), `payouts`, `bookings` (incoming/upcoming), `reviews`. No new tables required.

### MVP-now vs later
- **Now:** availability, at-a-glance stat cards, incoming/upcoming, recent sessions table, earnings + payout history, feedback, profile-health checklist.
- **Later:** performance analytics (views/plays/conversion), messaging, goal-setting.

---

## 2. Customer (client) dashboard

**Purpose:** get back into a conversation fast, manage bookings, and find receipts — low-pressure, warm, reassuring.

### Sections / widgets
| Section | Shows | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Resume / quick start** | "Talk now" entry + **next upcoming session** ("Next session: Tue 7:00pm with Maria") | Most-common need at the top. |
| **Favorite listeners** | Saved listeners with voice-intro play + **"Talk now / Rebook"** | Needs a small new `favorites` table (§5). |
| **Upcoming bookings** | Time, listener, block length, with **reschedule / cancel** | From `bookings`; respect the cancel policy in `SPEC.md` §5. |
| **Past sessions** | Table: date, listener, duration, amount, "Rebook" · "Leave/See review" | From `sessions` + `reviews`. |
| **Receipts / contributions** | Payment history with downloadable receipts | Label adapts to fee vs donation model. |
| **Payment & settings** | Manage payment method, notifications, language, profile | From `profiles` + payment adapter. |
| **Help & safety** | Always-visible Help; the persistent **"companionship, not therapy / crisis support"** link | Required on every screen. |

### Key actions
Talk now / rebook · favorite a listener · reschedule or cancel · leave a rating + tip · download a receipt · update payment/settings.

### Data
`bookings`, `sessions`, `payments`, `reviews`, `profiles`, **+ new `favorites`**.

### MVP-now vs later
- **Now:** resume/next session, upcoming + past bookings, receipts, payment/settings, help/safety.
- **Later:** favorites (small schema add — could be now if quick), spending summary, notification preferences detail.

---

## 3. Admin dashboard

**Purpose:** run the marketplace safely — approve supply, watch health, act on problems. The MVP shipped "provider approval only"; this expands it.

### Layout — three KPI tiers (from marketplace research)
| Tier | Cadence | Metrics for "Heard" |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategic** | Monthly | Total session value (GMV) · platform revenue (commission) · active providers · active customers · avg rating / NPS |
| **Operational** | Weekly | Booking→session conversion · **provider activation** (approved → first session) · session completion rate · supply/demand balance (available listeners vs requests) |
| **Alert** | Real-time / daily | **Approval backlog** · open reports/disputes · provider churn · cancellation/no-show rate · failed payments |

### Operational tools (sections)
| Section | Function | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Provider approvals** | Queue of `pending` providers + voice intro → Approve / Reject / Suspend (sets status + bg-check) | **MVP already built** — surface it here. |
| **Reports & safety** | Inbox of `reports` rows → review, contact, suspend | Table exists; **add the review UI now** (this is the safety backbone). |
| **Users** | Search customers/providers; view detail; suspend/reinstate | Add now (basic). |
| **Sessions & payments** | Recent sessions, payment/payout volume, refunds | Add now (read-only first). |
| **Config** | **Commission rate** (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`), content policy toggles | Read from config; editable later. |

### Data
Aggregations over `sessions`, `bookings`, `payments`, `payouts`, `providers`, `profiles`, `reviews`, `reports`. Implement as SQL **views** (`admin_metrics_*`) so the UI just reads them — see §5.

### MVP-now vs later
- **Now:** approvals (exists), strategic + alert stat cards, reports/safety review UI, basic user management, read-only sessions/payments.
- **Later:** editable config, trend charts (with accessible table fallbacks), CSV export, segmented analytics.

> **Note on scope:** `SPEC.md` deferred the moderation UI. Since you're building dashboards now, the **reports/safety review UI is the highest-value addition** — it's how you protect blind providers from abusive callers. Recommend pulling it forward into this milestone.

---

## 4. Accessibility acceptance criteria (all three, enforced)

- Every metric is a labeled number or a semantic table; any chart has a table + text-summary equivalent.
- Tables: `<th scope>`, `<thead>`, caption; sortable controls are keyboard-operable and announce sort state.
- No color-only status (approved/pending/suspended, available/offline, paid/failed all carry text + icon).
- Keyboard-only walkthrough of each dashboard succeeds; visible focus throughout; live-region announcements for toggles and async updates.
- axe passes on each dashboard screen in component tests (per `CLAUDE.md` definition of done).

---

## 5. Schema & query additions

**New tables (small):**
```sql
favorites (id, customer_id → profiles, provider_id → providers, created_at)   -- customer dashboard
notifications (id, user_id, type, payload jsonb, read_at, created_at)         -- optional, powers activity feeds
```
RLS: a customer sees only their own favorites/notifications; providers their own notifications.

**Admin metrics as SQL views** (so the UI reads, not computes):
`admin_metrics_strategic` (GMV, revenue, active counts), `admin_metrics_operational` (conversion, activation, completion, supply/demand), `admin_metrics_alerts` (backlog, open reports, churn, cancellations, failed payments). Keep all money in cents.

**No new external integrations** — dashboards run fully in `mock` mode.

---

## 6. Build summary (what to do this milestone)

1. **Listener dashboard** (priority, accessibility-first): availability, stat cards, incoming/upcoming, sessions table, earnings + payouts, feedback, profile-health.
2. **Customer dashboard:** resume/next, upcoming + past, receipts, settings, help/safety (+ `favorites` if quick).
3. **Admin dashboard:** keep approvals; add strategic/alert stat cards, **reports/safety review UI**, basic user management, read-only sessions/payments; metrics via SQL views.
4. Add `favorites` (+ optional `notifications`) tables with RLS; add the `admin_metrics_*` views.
5. Meet §4 accessibility criteria; axe + keyboard pass on every dashboard screen.

---

## Sources
- [Fiverr — Freelancer dashboard (provider patterns)](https://help.fiverr.com/hc/en-us/articles/360011653458-Freelancer-dashboard-for-web-and-mobile-app)
- [Sharetribe — Key marketplace metrics](https://www.sharetribe.com/academy/measure-your-success-key-marketplace-metrics/)
- [Origami — Marketplace KPIs & tiers (2026)](https://origami-marketplace.com/en-gb/multi-vendor-marketplace-kpis/)
- [The Startup Deck — Customer account dashboard best practices](https://www.thestartupdeck.com/post/customer-account-dashboard)
- [The A11Y Collective — Accessible data visualizations checklist](https://www.a11y-collective.com/blog/accessible-charts/)
- [AFixt — Accessible data tables (WCAG)](https://afixt.com/how-to-create-accessible-data-tables-best-practices-for-web-developers/)

-- =====================================================================
-- M10 — dashboard foundation: favorites + notifications tables (RLS), and
-- admin_metrics_* SQL views (computed in SQL, read by the UI). All money cents.
-- =====================================================================

-- ---- favorites (customer dashboard) ---------------------------------
create table public.favorites (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  customer_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  provider_id uuid not null references public.providers (id) on delete cascade,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (customer_id, provider_id)
);

create index favorites_customer_idx on public.favorites (customer_id);

create trigger favorites_set_updated_at
  before update on public.favorites
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

alter table public.favorites enable row level security;

create policy "favorites_select_own"
  on public.favorites for select
  using (customer_id = auth.uid() or public.is_admin());
create policy "favorites_insert_own"
  on public.favorites for insert
  with check (customer_id = auth.uid());
create policy "favorites_delete_own"
  on public.favorites for delete
  using (customer_id = auth.uid());

-- ---- notifications (optional; powers activity feeds) ----------------
create table public.notifications (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id    uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  type       text not null,
  payload    jsonb not null default '{}',
  read_at    timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index notifications_user_idx on public.notifications (user_id, read_at);

create trigger notifications_set_updated_at
  before update on public.notifications
  for each row execute function public.set_updated_at();

alter table public.notifications enable row level security;

create policy "notifications_select_own"
  on public.notifications for select
  using (user_id = auth.uid() or public.is_admin());
create policy "notifications_update_own"
  on public.notifications for update
  using (user_id = auth.uid())
  with check (user_id = auth.uid());

-- =====================================================================
-- Admin metric views. Computed in SQL so the UI just reads them. Money in
-- cents. Read server-side via the service-role client behind an admin route
-- guard; access is revoked from anon/authenticated so non-admins can't query
-- the aggregates directly.
-- =====================================================================

create view public.admin_metrics_strategic as
select
  coalesce((select sum(total_price_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as gmv_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(commission_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as revenue_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(provider_earnings_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as provider_earnings_cents,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved')::int as active_providers,
  (select count(distinct customer_id) from public.bookings)::int as active_customers,
  coalesce((select round(avg(rating)::numeric, 2) from public.reviews), 0)::numeric as avg_rating;

create view public.admin_metrics_operational as
select
  (select count(*) from public.bookings)::int as total_bookings,
  (select count(*) from public.sessions where status = 'completed')::int as completed_sessions,
  case
    when (select count(*) from public.bookings) > 0
      then round(
        (select count(*) from public.sessions where status = 'completed')::numeric
        / (select count(*) from public.bookings) * 100, 1)
    else 0
  end as booking_to_session_pct,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved')::int as approved_providers,
  (select count(distinct provider_id) from public.sessions where status = 'completed')::int as activated_providers,
  case
    when (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved') > 0
      then round(
        (select count(distinct provider_id) from public.sessions where status = 'completed')::numeric
        / (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved') * 100, 1)
    else 0
  end as provider_activation_pct,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved' and is_available_now)::int as available_now,
  (select count(*) from public.bookings where status in ('confirmed', 'in_progress'))::int as open_requests;

create view public.admin_metrics_alerts as
select
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'pending')::int as approval_backlog,
  (select count(*) from public.reports where status = 'open')::int as open_reports,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'suspended')::int as suspended_providers,
  (select count(*) from public.bookings where status = 'cancelled')::int as cancelled_bookings,
  case
    when (select count(*) from public.bookings) > 0
      then round(
        (select count(*) from public.bookings where status = 'cancelled')::numeric
        / (select count(*) from public.bookings) * 100, 1)
    else 0
  end as cancellation_pct,
  (select count(*) from public.payments where status = 'failed')::int as failed_payments;

revoke all on public.admin_metrics_strategic from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on public.admin_metrics_operational from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on public.admin_metrics_alerts from anon, authenticated;

Resuming M13. I confirmed a **real pre-existing security hole**: the M0 `profiles` RLS lets a user PATCH their own `role` to `admin` (privilege escalation) — and now there'll be a `is_suspended` flag they could clear too. The M13 migration will fix both with a guard trigger. (Customer c1's role got escalated in that test; the upcoming `db reset` restores it from seed.)

Let me write the M13 migration — `is_suspended` + the profiles column guard.

input.content:
-- =====================================================================
-- M13 — admin dashboard support: user suspension + a profiles column guard
-- that also closes a privilege-escalation hole (a user could previously PATCH
-- their own profiles.role to 'admin' via the owner-scoped RLS update policy).
-- =====================================================================

alter table public.profiles
  add column is_suspended boolean not null default false;

-- Freeze privileged profile columns for ordinary authenticated users. Trusted
-- server writes (service role → auth.uid() is null) and admins pass through.
create or replace function public.guard_profile_privileged_columns()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = public
as $$
begin
  if auth.uid() is null or public.is_admin() then
    return new;
  end if;
  -- A user editing their own profile cannot change their role or un-suspend
  -- themselves.
  new.role         := old.role;
  new.is_suspended := old.is_suspended;
  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger profiles_guard_privileged
  before update on public.profiles
  for each row execute function public.guard_profile_privileged_columns();

-- Suspended customers can't be active. Exclude them from the "active customers"
-- strategic metric.
create or replace view public.admin_metrics_strategic as
select
  coalesce((select sum(total_price_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as gmv_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(commission_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as revenue_cents,
  coalesce((select sum(provider_earnings_cents) from public.sessions where status = 'completed'), 0)::bigint as provider_earnings_cents,
  (select count(*) from public.providers where status = 'approved')::int as active_providers,
  (select count(distinct b.customer_id)
     from public.bookings b
     join public.profiles p on p.id = b.customer_id
    where p.is_suspended = false)::int as active_customers,
  coalesce((select round(avg(rating)::numeric, 2) from public.reviews), 0)::numeric as avg_rating;

revoke all on public.admin_metrics_strategic from anon, authenticated;

## n8n
This is the official MCP server for n8n, a workflow automation platform.

This MCP server provides tools to build n8n workflows programmatically using the n8n Workflow SDK.

To build n8n workflows, follow these steps in order:

1. Read the SDK reference: You MUST call get_sdk_reference (or use the n8n://workflow-sdk/reference resource) before writing workflow code. Do not guess SDK syntax.

2. Get suggested nodes: You MUST call get_suggested_nodes with all relevant workflow technique categories before searching for nodes. Use the recommendations, pattern hints, and configuration guidance to decide which nodes and patterns to use.

3. Discover nodes: Call search_nodes with queries for services you need (e.g., ["gmail", "slack", "schedule trigger"]), utility nodes (e.g., ["set", "if", "merge", "code"]), and suggested nodes you plan to use. Note the discriminators (resource/operation/mode) in the results.

4. Get type definitions: Call get_node_types with ALL node IDs you plan to use, including discriminators from search results. This returns the exact TypeScript parameter definitions. DO NOT skip this — guessing parameter names creates invalid workflows.

5. Write the workflow code using the SDK patterns from the reference and the exact parameter names from the type definitions. Follow the coding guidelines and design guidance sections of the SDK reference (retrieve them with get_sdk_reference using sections "guidelines" and "design").

6. Validate: Call validate_workflow with your full code. Fix any errors and re-validate until valid.

7. Create: Call create_workflow_from_code with the validated code to save the workflow to n8n. Include a short `description` (1-2 sentences) summarizing what the workflow does — this helps users find and understand their workflows.

8. Update: Call update_workflow with the workflow ID and a list of operations (addNode, removeNode, updateNodeParameters, setNodeParameter, renameNode, addConnection, removeConnection, setNodeCredential, setNodePosition, setNodeDisabled, setWorkflowMetad… [truncated]
