# Build Plan — "Heard"

## Context

We're building **Heard**: a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion
listeners who are all legally blind or visually impaired. Non-clinical companionship — never
therapy. The product's whole point is accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body contrast) and
the dignity of providers.

The working directory is **empty** (greenfield). I have the full source of truth:
- `SPEC.md` — architecture, data model, adapter pattern, pricing, routes, flows.
- `BUILD_PLAN.md` — milestones M0→M9.
- `CLAUDE.md` — golden rules (a11y, adapters-only, integer cents, RLS everywhere, validate at boundary, server-first, i18n copy, safety framing).
- Design brief + design system: exact color/type tokens (`colors_and_type.css`), voice/microcopy rules, and a working prototype (`ui.jsx`, `data.jsx`, 11 screens) to match the visual language.

**Decisions locked with you:** (1) **Local Supabase CLI** — real SQL migrations + RLS + seed,
runnable via `supabase db reset`. (2) **Milestone checkpoints** — build M0, stop and show it runs,
then continue milestone by milestone.

**Toolchain gap found:** Node 26 / npm 11 / git / Homebrew are present, but the **Supabase CLI and
any container runtime (Docker/Colima/Podman) are missing**. Local Supabase needs a container runtime.
M0 therefore includes a headless install via Homebrew (`supabase` + `colima` + `docker` CLI) — no
Docker Desktop GUI required.

The reference material lives under `_refs/` (extracted from the two zips). It is reference only and
will not ship; I'll keep it out of the app and gitignore it (or remove it before handoff).

---

## Stack & conventions (apply on every milestone)

- Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript `strict` · Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage) · Tailwind · Zod · Vitest + RTL + Playwright.
- Design tokens from `colors_and_type.css` become Tailwind theme + CSS vars in `globals.css`. Lora (display) + Nunito Sans (body), 18px body floor, ≥48px tap targets, 3px `#1B6FB0` focus ring never removed.
- All external services through adapters only (`getPayments/getCalls/getBackgroundCheck`); never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly.
- All money integer cents; all pricing math only in `lib/pricing.ts`; commission from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`.
- RLS on every table; service-role key server-only. Zod-validate + role/ownership-check every server action.
- All user-facing copy via `messages/en.json`. Persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" affordance on every page.
- Each milestone ends green: `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, and an **axe** pass on any new screen.

---

## This session = M0 only (then checkpoint)

**Goal of M0:** a user can sign up / sign in as customer or provider, role persists, every UI
primitive passes axe, app shell + safety affordance render, CI scripts green.

### M0.0 — Toolchain (one-time, needs your approval to install)
- `brew install supabase/tap/supabase` (Supabase CLI).
- `brew install colima docker` (headless container runtime + docker client), then `colima start`.
- Verify `supabase --version` and `docker info` work. (Colima pulls a small Linux VM image on first start — a few minutes.)

### M0.1 — Scaffold
- `create-next-app` (App Router, TS, Tailwind, ESLint) into the working dir.
- Add Prettier, Vitest + RTL + `jest-axe`, Playwright. `package.json` scripts: `dev/build/lint/typecheck/test/test:e2e`.
- `tsconfig` strict; ESLint + Prettier configs.
- GitHub Actions CI: typecheck + lint + test. `git init` + first commit.
- `.gitignore` includes `_refs/`, `.env*`, `node_modules`, `.next`.

### M0.2 — Supabase wiring
- `supabase init`. `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts` (SSR `@supabase/ssr`: browser client, server client w/ cookies, middleware session refresh).
- `.env.example` exactly per SPEC §9 (URL, anon, service-role, `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`, `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard`, commented real-integration keys). Write local `.env.local` from `supabase start` output.
- Minimal `profiles` migration here (full data model is M1) so sign-up can create a profile row and auth works end-to-end this milestone.

### M0.3 — Design tokens + i18n
- `app/globals.css`: import Lora + Nunito Sans; port every `--token` from `colors_and_type.css`; semantic defaults (body bg/color/font, heading font, universal `:focus-visible` ring, reduced-motion block).
- `tailwind.config.ts`: map tokens to theme (colors, fontFamily, radii, shadows, spacing) so utilities and tokens agree.
- `messages/en.json` + tiny `lib/i18n.ts` `t()` helper (typed key lookup). Seed with microcopy verbatim from the design README (hero, trust line, reassurance, safety line, availability states, empty states). **No hard-coded UI strings after this.**

### M0.4 — UI primitives (`components/ui/`), accessible by construction
Ported from the prototype's `ui.jsx` to typed React + Tailwind/tokens:
`Button` (primary/amber/ghost/danger/quiet, icon+label, ≥48px), `Field`/`Input`, `Select`,
`Card`, `Dialog` (focus-trap, Esc, scrim), `Toast` + live-region announcer, `Tag`/`Chip`
(`aria-pressed`, check icon), `Avatar` (initial tile), `FocusRing` util, plus product primitives
`Availability` (icon+text, never color alone), `VoicePlayer` (simulated, labeled), `SafetyNote`.
Icons via `lucide-react`, always with text/`aria-label` — no icon-only controls.

### M0.5 — Auth + app shell
- `/signin`, `/signup` (server actions + Zod). Sign-up has **role selection** (customer/provider). On sign-up: create `profiles` row; provider also creates a `providers` row `status=pending` (provider insert via service-role server action).
- `lib/auth.ts`: `getUser()`, `getProfile()`, `requireRole()`.
- App shell: header/nav + persistent SafetyNote affordance; route groups `(marketing)/(auth)/(customer)/(provider)/(admin)`; middleware redirects by auth/role. Crisis-support dialog reachable from the affordance.

### M0.6 — Tests + green gate
- Unit: `t()` helper, role-selection schema.
- Component + **axe**: each `components/ui` primitive, `/signin`, `/signup`.
- Run `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`. Smoke-run `dev`.

**M0 done when:** sign up/in as either role works, role persists in `profiles`/`providers`, every
primitive + auth screen passes axe, CI scripts pass locally. → **Stop, show you it runs, get sign-off for M1.**

---

## Remaining milestones (later sessions, same checkpoint cadence)

- **M1** — Full data model migrations + RLS for all SPEC §4 tables; `seed.sql` (6 providers + admin + customer); `lib/db/queries.ts` + `lib/validation/schemas.ts`. Done when `supabase db reset` applies clean and RLS is verified.
- **M2** — Integration adapters (payments/calls/background-check): `interface/mock/real/index`; `lib/pricing.ts` pure (blocks, overage, 5% commission, tips, half-up). Unit tests cover every mock + all pricing cases.
- **M3** — Provider side: audio-first `/provider/onboarding` (voice intro → Storage, topics/languages, prices, availability, `backgroundCheck.initiate()`), `/provider/dashboard` (Available-now toggle, sessions, earnings, rating). Keyboard/SR-verified.
- **M4** — Admin `/admin/providers` approval queue (approve/reject/suspend), role-guarded.
- **M5** — Customer discovery + booking: `/`, `/browse` (filters + voice players), `/listeners/[id]`, `/book/[providerId]` → `authorizeHold` + `booking` confirmed.
- **M6** — Session lifecycle: `/session/[id]` pre-call → mock call (count-up timer, mute, captions, end), provider mirror; on end → pricing → `capture` → `session` completed.
- **M7** — `/session/[id]/summary` rating + optional tip + receipt; weekly mock payouts; payout history.
- **M8** — Full a11y + visual polish pass (SPEC §10): focus order, live regions, 200% zoom, reduced motion, contrast; safety affordance + minimal report hook on every page.
- **M9** — Tests/docs/handoff: unit + component + 2 Playwright E2E happy paths; `README.md`; verify `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to TODO stubs.

---

## Verification (M0)

1. `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test` → all green; axe assertions pass for every primitive + `/signin` + `/signup`.
2. `supabase start` up; `npm run dev`; in browser: sign up as **customer** → `profiles.role=customer`; sign up as **provider** → `profiles.role=provider` + `providers` row `status=pending`; sign out / sign in works; middleware blocks unauthed routes.
3. Manual keyboard-only pass of `/signup`: visible focus ring on every control, role selection operable, no icon-only buttons.
4. SafetyNote affordance visible on every rendered page; crisis dialog opens and is focus-trapped.

## Notes / risks
- Colima first-start downloads a VM image (a few minutes); if you'd rather not install a runtime, the fallback is the "defer DB" mode — but you chose local Supabase, so M0.0 installs it.
- `_refs/` is reference only; gitignored, never imported by app code.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.

This MCP server provides tools to build n8n workflows programmatically using the n8n Workflow SDK.

To build n8n workflows, follow these steps in order:

1. Read the SDK reference: You MUST call get_sdk_reference (or use the n8n://workflow-sdk/reference resource) before writing workflow code. Do not guess SDK syntax.

## M13 — Admin dashboard

Admin operations surface for Heard, plus a security hardening of the suspension/role surface.

### Screens
- **Overview** (`/admin`) — strategic / operational / alert StatCards read from the `admin_metrics_*` SQL views (no metric math in the UI) + commission config.
- **Approvals** (`/admin/providers`) — existing M4 queue.
- **Reports** (`/admin/reports`) — safety-report inbox: mark reviewed, suspend the reported user.
- **Users** (`/admin/users`) — searchable user table with suspend / reinstate (admins not actionable).
- **Activity** (`/admin/activity`) — read-only sessions / payments / payouts tables.

### Security / data
- New `profiles.is_suspended`; a `guard_profile_privileged_columns()` trigger freezes `role` + `is_suspended` for non-admin authenticated users (closes a role-escalation hole where a customer could PATCH their own `role`).
- Suspension enforced at booking creation and at call start (both parties).
- All admin metric views revoked from anon/authenticated; read via the service-role client behind `requireRole("admin")`.

### Adversarial review
A 5-lens review (security / correctness / a11y / money / reuse) with 2-skeptic verification found **13 issues — all 13 applied** (commit `376d785`). Highlights:
- **[HIGH]** reinstating a provider no longer auto-approves them — the approval/vetting gate can't be bypassed (verified end-to-end on a pending provider).
- `setUserSuspended` rejects admin targets server-side; `startSession` blocks if either party is suspended.
- `listUsers` double-quotes the ilike value, closing a PostgREST `.or()` filter-injection hole (verified the comma-injection payload now returns no rows).
- Activity-table statuses render localized labels + icons (no raw enum tokens); action buttons carry the subject name in their accessible name; users page announces a live result count.

############## DASHBOARDS_BUILD_PLAN.md — M14 section ##############
# Dashboards Build Plan — "Heard" (M10–M14)

Continues `BUILD_PLAN.md` after the M0–M9 MVP. Builds the fuller **Listener / Customer / Admin** dashboards per `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md`. Runs fully in **mock mode** — no new integrations. All the rules in `CLAUDE.md` still apply (accessibility WCAG 2.2 AA, adapter pattern, money in integer cents via `lib/pricing.ts`, RLS on every table).

**Kickoff prompt for Claude Code:**
> Read `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, then implement `DASHBOARDS_BUILD_PLAN.md` starting at **M10**, **one milestone at a time**. At the end of each: run typecheck, lint, tests, and an **axe pass on every dashboard screen**; show me how to verify it; wait for my go-ahead. Reuse the existing `components/ui`, schema, and `lib/pricing.ts`. Money stays in cents; add RLS to new tables; read admin metrics from SQL views, don't compute them in the UI.

Legend: each milestone has **Tasks** and **Done when** (acceptance criteria).

---

## M10 — Dashboard foundation (shared)
**Tasks**
- [ ] Migration: `favorites` (customer_id, provider_id) + RLS (owner-scoped); update `seed.sql`.
- [ ] Migration: `notifications` (user_id, type, payload, read_at) + RLS *(optional; powers activity feeds)*.
- [ ] Migration: SQL views `admin_metrics_strategic`, `admin_metrics_operational`, `admin_metrics_alerts` (all money in cents).
- [ ] Shared dashboard shell: role-aware layout + nav, landmarks/regions, and the persistent "companionship, not therapy / crisis support" link.
- [ ] Accessible primitives in `components/ui`: `StatCard` (labeled number), `DataTable` (semantic `<table>` with `<th scope>`, `<thead>`, caption; keyboard-operable sort that announces state), `StatusBadge` (text + icon, never color-only).
- [ ] Unit tests for the metric views/queries; axe tests for the primitives.

**Done when:** `supabase db reset` applies the new tables + views with seed data; primitives pass axe; RLS verified (a user cannot read another user's favorites/notifications).

---

## M11 — Listener (provider) dashboard  *[priority — accessibility-first]*
**Tasks**
- [ ] Availability section: reuse the MVP toggle (announce "You're available / offline" via live region) + next scheduled session.
- [ ] At-a-glance `StatCard`s: this week's earnings, pending/uncleared, next payout date, average rating, sessions this week.
- [ ] Incoming requests (Accept / Decline) + upcoming confirmed sessions (time, customer first name, block length).
- [ ] Recent sessions `DataTable`: date, duration, block + overage, earnings, rating.
- [ ] Earnings & payouts: balance, this month, lifetime; payout history table (period, amount, status).
- [ ] Feedback: recent reviews (rating, comment, tip).
- [ ] Profile-health checklist (voice intro, topics, languages, prices, availability; approval / background-check status) with edit links.

**Done when:** a seeded provider sees accurate earnings/sessions/feedback; a **keyboard-only + screen-reader walkthrough succeeds**; axe passes. Data maps to `providers`, `sessions`, `payouts`, `bookings`, `reviews` (no new tables).

---

## M12 — Customer (client) dashboard
**Tasks**
- [ ] Resume / quick-start: "Talk now" + a next-upcoming-session banner.
- [ ] Favorite listeners (uses `favorites`): list with voice-intro play + "Talk now / Rebook"; add/remove favorite from the profile and browse screens.
- [ ] Upcoming bookings with reschedule / cancel (respect the cancel policy in `SPEC.md` §5).
- [ ] Past sessions `DataTable`: date, listener, duration, amount, "Rebook" / leave-or-see review.
- [ ] Receipts / contributions: payment history with a downloadable receipt (label via `messages/en.json` so fee-vs-donation wording can switch).
- [ ] Payment & settings (method, notifications, language, profile); always-visible Help + safety link.

**Done when:** a seeded customer can favorite a listener, rebook, reschedule/cancel, and view receipts; axe + keyboard pass on every screen.

---

## M13 — Admin dashboard
**Tasks**
- [ ] Fold the existing approvals queue into the dashboard shell.
- [ ] Strategic + alert `StatCard`s from `admin_metrics_*` views: GMV (session value), platform revenue, active providers, active customers, approval backlog, open reports, churn, cancellations, failed payments.
- [ ] Operational metrics: booking→session conversion, provider activation, completion rate, supply/demand balance.
- [ ] **Reports & safety review UI**: inbox of `reports` → review, contact, suspend (pulled forward from `SPEC.md` §12 — the safety backbone for protecting blind providers).
- [ ] Basic user management: search, view detail, suspend / reinstate.
- [ ] Read-only sessions and payments/payouts views.
- [ ] Config panel: display commission rate (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`); editing is later.

**Done when:** admin sees live metrics from the views, can action a report and suspend a user, and the approval flow still works; non-admins are blocked (RLS + route guard); any chart has a table + text-summary fallback; axe passes.

---

## M14 — Accessibility, tests, polish
**Tasks**
- [ ] Full pass against `DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md` §4 on all three dashboards: semantic tables, no color-only status, visible focus, live-region announcements, reduced density.
- [ ] Component tests + axe for each dashboard; extend Playwright: (a) provider views earnings; (b) customer favorites → rebook; (c) admin actions a report.
- [ ] Warm/consistent styling; empty / loading / error states; quick performance check on the metric views.

**Done when:** every dashboard screen passes axe and a keyboard-only walkthrough; the new E2E paths and CI are green.

---

**Notes**
- Continues the M-numbering — append these to `BUILD_PLAN.md` or keep this file alongside it.
- Mock mode only; no Stripe/Zoom/Checkr work here.
- Build order is deliberate: foundation → listener (highest stakes for accessibility) → customer → admin → hardening.

content.content:
############## DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §4 ##############
**Accessibility for dashboards is the hard part — especially the Listener view, whose users are blind.** From the research, apply these as rules:
- Prefer **labeled "stat cards" (plain numbers) and semantic data tables** over charts. If a chart is used, it must be paired with an equivalent **data table** and a one-line **text summary of the takeaway**.
- Tables use real `<table>` semantics: `<th scope=…>`, `<thead>`, captions. Screen readers must announce headers.
- **Never encode meaning in color alone** — add text/icon/pattern. Contrast ≥ 4.5:1.
- Everything keyboard-operable, logical tab order, visible focus; state changes announced via live regions (e.g., "You're now available").
- **Reduce density.** Use filters and progressive disclosure; don't crowd the screen. This helps everyone and is essential for screen-reader users.

**Money & framing.** All amounts in integer cents via `lib/pricing.ts`. Labels adapt to the eventual model: "Earnings" (listener), "Receipts/Contributions" (customer) — keep copy in `messages/en.json` so the fee-vs-donation wording can switch.

---

## 1. Listener (provider) dashboard — *the priority*

**Purpose:** one calm place to go available, see who's coming, track earnings, and keep their profile healthy. Must be flawless by screen reader.

### Sections / widgets
| Section | Shows | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Availability** | Big **"Available now"** toggle with text state ("You're available" / "You're offline"); next scheduled session | Already in MVP. Toggle announces state via live region. |
| **At a glance (stat cards)** | This week's earnings · pending (uncleared) · next payout date · average rating · sessions this week | Plain labeled numbers, not charts. |
| **Incoming & upcoming** | Pending requests (Accept / Decline) + upcoming confirmed sessions (time, customer first name, block length) | Accept/Decline are large, clearly labeled. |
| **Recent sessions** | Table: date, duration, block + overage, earnings, rating left | Semantic table; sortable optional. |
| **Earnings & payouts** | Balance, this month, lifetime; payout history (date, period, amount, status) | Maps to `sessions` + `payouts`. |
| **Feedback** | Recent reviews (rating + comment + tip) | From `reviews`. |
| **Profile health** | Completeness checklist: voice intro ✓, topics, languages, prices, availability; **approval / background-check status** | Drives activation; links to edit. |
| **Simple performance** *(later)* | Profile views, voice-intro plays, bookings, conversion (last 7 days) | Keep minimal; numbers + table, no dense viz. |

### Key actions
Go available/offline · accept/decline a request · join a session · edit profile/voice intro/prices/availability · view payout detail · respond to a review.

### Data (existing tables)
`providers` (status, rating, prices, availability), `sessions` (earnings, durations, counts), `payouts`, `bookings` (incoming/upcoming), `reviews`. No new tables required.

### MVP-now vs later
- **Now:** availability, at-a-glance stat cards, incoming/upcoming, recent sessions table, earnings + payout history, feedback, profile-health checklist.
- **Later:** performance analytics (views/plays/conversion), messaging, goal-setting.

---

## 2. Customer (client) dashboard

**Purpose:** get back into a conversation fast, manage bookings, and find receipts — low-pressure, warm, reassuring.

### Sections / widgets
| Section | Shows | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Resume / quick start** | "Talk now" entry + **next upcoming session** ("Next session: Tue 7:00pm with Maria") | Most-common need at the top. |
| **Favorite listeners** | Saved listeners with voice-intro play + **"Talk now / Rebook"** | Needs a small new `favorites` table (§5). |
| **Upcoming bookings** | Time, listener, block length, with **reschedule / cancel** | From `bookings`; respect the cancel policy in `SPEC.md` §5. |
| **Past sessions** | Table: date, listener, duration, amount, "Rebook" · "Leave/See review" | From `sessions` + `reviews`. |
| **Receipts / contributions** | Payment history with downloadable receipts | Label adapts to fee vs donation model. |
| **Payment & settings** | Manage payment method, notifications, language, profile | From `profiles` + payment adapter. |
| **Help & safety** | Always-visible Help; the persistent **"companionship, not therapy / crisis support"** link | Required on every screen. |

### Key actions
Talk now / rebook · favorite a listener · reschedule or cancel · leave a rating + tip · download a receipt · update payment/settings.

### Data
`bookings`, `sessions`, `payments`, `reviews`, `profiles`, **+ new `favorites`**.

### MVP-now vs later
- **Now:** resume/next session, upcoming + past bookings, receipts, payment/settings, help/safety.
- **Later:** favorites (small schema add — could be now if quick), spending summary, notification preferences detail.

---

## 3. Admin dashboard

**Purpose:** run the marketplace safely — approve supply, watch health, act on problems. The MVP shipped "provider approval only"; this expands it.

### Layout — three KPI tiers (from marketplace research)
| Tier | Cadence | Metrics for "Heard" |
|---|---|---|
| **Strategic** | Monthly | Total session value (GMV) · platform revenue (commission) · active providers · active customers · avg rating / NPS |
| **Operational** | Weekly | Booking→session conversion · **provider activation** (approved → first session) · session completion rate · supply/demand balance (available listeners vs requests) |
| **Alert** | Real-time / daily | **Approval backlog** · open reports/disputes · provider churn · cancellation/no-show rate · failed payments |

### Operational tools (sections)
| Section | Function | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Provider approvals** | Queue of `pending` providers + voice intro → Approve / Reject / Suspend (sets status + bg-check) | **MVP already built** — surface it here. |
| **Reports & safety** | Inbox of `reports` rows → review, contact, suspend | Table exists; **add the review UI now** (this is the safety backbone). |
| **Users** | Search customers/providers; view detail; suspend/reinstate | Add now (basic). |
| **Sessions & payments** | Recent sessions, payment/payout volume, refunds | Add now (read-only first). |
| **Config** | **Commission rate** (`PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE`), content policy toggles | Read from config; editable later. |

### Data
Aggregations over `sessions`, `bookings`, `payments`, `payouts`, `providers`, `profiles`, `reviews`, `reports`. Implement as SQL **views** (`admin_metrics_*`) so the UI just reads them — see §5.

### MVP-now vs later

=== reviews table schema ===
create table public.reviews (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  session_id  uuid references public.sessions (id) on delete set null,
  customer_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  provider_id uuid not null references public.providers (id) on delete cascade,
  rating      integer not null,
  comment     text,
  tip_cents   integer not null default 0,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  constraint reviews_rating_range check (rating between 1 and 5),
  constraint reviews_tip_nonneg check (tip_cents >= 0)
);

**Heard** is a two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind/visually impaired — non-clinical companionship, never therapy. Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body) and provider dignity are the whole point. Stack: Next.js 16 App Router + TS strict + Supabase + Tailwind v4 + Zod + Vitest/RTL/jest-axe + Playwright. External services (payments/calls/background-check) are mocked behind adapters (`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`); money is integer cents; all pricing in `lib/pricing.ts`; all copy via `messages/en.json`.

Governing docs live at repo root: `SPEC.md`, `BUILD_PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md`. Design tokens are in `app/globals.css` (@theme), ported from the design system.

**Working agreement:** build milestone-by-milestone (M0→M9) with a **checkpoint** after each — stop, show it runs, get sign-off before the next.

**Progress:**
- **M0 (done, committed `4066c54` on main):** scaffold, design tokens, accessible UI primitives, i18n, email+password auth with customer/provider role selection (role persisted via a Postgres `handle_new_user` trigger that also creates a `providers` row status=pending), RLS on profiles/providers, SSR clients + `proxy.ts` (Next 16 renamed middleware→proxy) route guards, app shell + persistent crisis-safety affordance. 25 tests green.
- **M1 (done, PR #4):** full data model for all SPEC §4 tables + RLS on every table; `seed.sql` (admin + customer + 6 approved providers, all sign in with `password123`); `lib/db/queries.ts` (RLS-enforced reads, public provider reads omit bg_check_ref/payout_account_ref) + entity Zod schemas. `supabase db reset` clean; RLS verified. Seed gotcha: insert `auth.users` set-based with empty-string token columns (confirmation_token etc.) or GoTrue 500s on login; add an `auth.identities` row so accounts can sign in; no dollar-quoted functions in seed.sql (the runner's batcher breaks them).
- **M2 (done, PR #5):** integration adapters under `lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/{interface,mock,real,index}.ts` — call `getPayments()/getCalls()/getBackgroundCheck()`, never import mock/real directly; real stubs throw `// TODO` errors. `lib/pricing.ts` is the only place for money math (pure, integer cents, half-up commission from config). Payments mock takes an injected Supabase client (no server-only) so it's unit-testable. 66 tests.
- **M3 (done, PR #6):** provider onboarding (4-step audio-first → Storage voice-intro bucket, topics/languages, prices, availability, mock bg-check) + dashboard (Available-now switch, earnings, rating). Guard trigger freezes privileged provider columns so providers can't self-approve.
- **M4 (done, PR #7):** admin `/admin/providers` queue with voice-intro playback + approve/reject/suspend (service-role writes); role-guarded. VoicePlayer plays real audio via signed URLs. Verified: approve → browse-eligible; non-admins redirected.
- **M5 (done, PR #8):** `/browse` (approved-only, URL filters, voice players), `/listeners/[id]`, `/book/[providerId]` (createBooking → priceForBlock → payments.authorizeHold → confirmed), `/account`. Verified: booking confirmed + $24 authorized hold in payments ledger. 77 tests.
- **M6 (done, PR #9):** session lifecycle — pre-call → mock call (count-up timer = source of truth, mute, captions, end), provider mirror; on end → computeSessionAccounting → payments.capture → completed. Verified: $24 total / $1.20 commission / $22.80 earnings, payment captured.
- **M7 (done, PR #10):** rating + optional tip (no commission) on the summary; recompute provider rating; weekly mock payouts (admin "Run weekly payouts") shown on provider dashboard.
- **M8 (done, PR #11):** Report-a-problem hook writing to `reports` (RLS reporter-owned), shown in the global SafetyBanner when signed in; booking-confirmed live region; a11y verification.
- **M9 (done, PR #12):** Playwright E2E (2 happy paths pass), README handoff (seeded accounts password123, adapter-swap guide), verified INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real `next build` compiles all 16 routes to TODO stubs.

Done. Both remaining milestones are shipped and merged — the full **M10–M14 dashboards phase is complete.**

## M13 — Admin dashboard ([PR #17](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/17), merged)
Adversarial review found **13 issues, all 13 fixed**. The headline one was a **HIGH** correctness/security bug I verified end-to-end in the browser: reinstating a suspended provider unconditionally set their status to `approved` — so a *pending* or *rejected* listener could be silently auto-approved, bypassing the vetting gate. Now only the `approved⇄suspended` pair toggles. Also: server-side guard so admins can't be suspended, both-party suspension enforcement at call start, a verified **PostgREST filter-injection fix** in user search (`,role.eq.admin` breakout — confirmed neutralized with a live curl test), localized activity-table statuses with icons, and disambiguated button accessible names.

## M14 — Accessibility, tests & polish ([PR #18](https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard/pull/18), merged)
Ran a 10-screen adversarial WCAG audit (44 raw confirmations) and triaged to the genuine fixes — **computing every contrast ratio against the real `@theme` tokens** rather than trusting the model's guesses:
- **Real AA failures fixed:** `StatusBadge` success (4.27:1) and warning (3.08:1) tones → darker shades (5.99:1 / 5.60:1), verified in the built CSS. Icons added to the last colour-only badges. DataTable sort announcement → i18n.
- **False positives correctly rejected:** `ink-soft` actually measures 5.2–6.0:1 (pass); `toast()` already announces to SR; sort buttons already carry names; star ratings already have sr-only text.
- **Error states:** accessible `app/error.tsx` + `app/not-found.tsx` (404 verified in-browser, keeps the safety affordance — screenshot above).
- **Seed enrichment:** a real Casey↔Maya history (3 sessions, payments, payouts, a tip, an upcoming booking — integer cents per `lib/pricing.ts`) so **every dashboard now shows real data** and admin GMV/revenue are non-zero. Aggregates verified against the metric views.
- **E2E:** 3 new dashboard paths (provider earnings, customer favorite→rebook, admin actions a report) **plus** I found and fixed a *pre-existing broken* `customer-journey` test — it looked for "join the call" on `/account`, but the dashboards redesign had renamed that CTA to "Join". It was silently failing on `main` (E2E isn't in `npm test`).

**All gates green:** typecheck · lint · build · **104** unit/component tests (incl. axe) · **5/5** Playwright E2E.

The Heard build is now complete through the dashboards phase: full MVP loop (M0–M9) plus the Listener/Customer/Admin dashboards (M10–M14), all merged to `main`. Out-of-scope fast-follows (real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, native mobile, subscriptions, editable commission) remain intentionally deferred with schema + adapters ready.

One thing I deliberately **did not** do, and would flag for a future pass: the app-wide `<Link><Button>` CTA pattern produces nested interactive elements (`<a><button>`). It's functional and pervasive across every route, so fixing it belongs in a dedicated `Button`-polymorphism refactor rather than smuggled into this milestone.

product). Stack: Next.js 16 App Router, TS strict, Supabase (Postgres+Auth+Storage), Tailwind v4,
Zod, Vitest/RTL/jest-axe, Playwright. Mock mode (INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock) via adapters in
lib/integrations/*. Money is integer cents in lib/pricing.ts. The MVP (M0–M9) and the
Listener/Customer/Admin dashboards (M10–M14) are all built and merged to main.

Governing docs at repo root: SPEC.md, BUILD_PLAN.md, DASHBOARDS_BUILD_PLAN.md,
DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md. READ the docs relevant to your dimension AND the
actual code (use Read/Grep/Glob). Report only REAL, grounded gaps — things actually missing,
partial, risky, or debt — not hypotheticals. For each, give a concrete file/doc pointer and a
specific recommendation. Be exhaustive within your dimension; it's fine to return many findings.`

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['findings'],
  properties: { findings: { type: 'array', items: {
    type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
    required: ['title', 'status', 'severity', 'effort', 'detail', 'pointer', 'recommendation'],
    properties: {
      title: { type: 'string' },
      status: { type: 'string', enum: ['missing', 'partial', 'risk', 'debt', 'polish'] },
      severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
      effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L'] },
      detail: { type: 'string' },
      pointer: { type: 'string' },
      recommendation: { type: 'string' },
    },
  } } },
}

const DIMS = [
  { key: 'spec-coverage', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Spec coverage & feature completeness. Read SPEC.md (all sections, esp. §5 booking/cancel policy, §11 routes, §12 out-of-scope), BUILD_PLAN.md, DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md (the "later" columns + moderation/notifications), and CLAUDE.md "Out of scope". Identify what is specified-but-unbuilt or only partially built: the notifications table (is it created? used?), moderation/reporting beyond the minimal hook, reschedule/cancel edge cases vs SPEC §5, the downloadable receipt (real artifact vs link?), language/i18n actually switchable, performance analytics, messaging, spending summary, subscriptions. Distinguish "intentionally deferred (documented)" from "gap".' },
  { key: 'security-rls', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Security, RLS & data protection. Read all supabase/migrations/*.sql RLS policies + guard triggers, lib/supabase/* (client/server/admin/proxy), every "use server" action under app/**/actions.ts, and lib/db/queries.ts. Hunt for: tables missing RLS or with overly-broad policies, service-role key exposure to client, missing ownership/role checks in server actions, IDOR, injection (PostgREST .or/.filter), privileged-column writes, public reads leaking private fields (bg_check_ref/payout_account_ref), auth boundary holes in proxy.ts, and whether is_suspended is fully enforced everywhere it should be.' },
  { key: 'prod-readiness', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Production readiness & ops. Read .github/workflows/*, package.json scripts, .env.example, next.config.*, README.md, supabase/config.toml, and lib/integrations/*/real.ts. Assess: CI completeness (does it run typecheck/lint/test/build/e2e? does e2e have a DB?), env var completeness + secret handling, the INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real swap path (do real.ts stubs exist for Stripe/Zoom/Checkr and does the app compile with real?), deploy story (Vercel + Supabase migrations), error monitoring/logging, rate limiting, seed-vs-prod data safety, and any missing operational guardrails.' },
  { key: 'test-coverage', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Test coverage & quality gates. Read tests/** (unit, component, e2e), vitest/playwright configs, and cross-reference against app code. Identify untested surfaces: server actions (booking/session/review/admin), lib/db/queries (RLS behavior), pricing edge cases (overage rounding, commission, tips, cancellation), adapters, axe coverage per dashboard screen, and E2E gaps (cancel/reschedule, suspension enforcement, payout run, error/404). Note any flaky-by-design tests or missing assertions.' },
  { key: 'accessibility', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Accessibility (the product\'s whole point — WCAG 2.2 AA floor, AAA body). Read components/ui/*, the session/call screens (app/(customer)/session/**, app/(provider)/provider/session/**), Dialog, forms, and SPEC.md §10. Beyond the M14 dashboard pass, find remaining gaps: the app-wide <Link><Button> nested-interactive (<a><button>) pattern, reduced-motion handling, 200% zoom/reflow, focus order + focus trap in Dialog, live-region coverage on the live call (timer/captions/mute), form error association, skip-link correctness, and any icon-only controls. Verify contrast claims against the real @theme tokens in app/globals.css — do not guess ratios.' },
  { key: 'code-quality', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Code quality & tech debt. Skim the codebase for: duplicated logic that should be shared, dead code / orphaned i18n keys, error swallowing (empty catches, ignored results), any-typing or unsafe casts, inconsistent patterns across the three dashboards, the Link>Button polymorphism debt, magic numbers/literals (esp. money or commission outside lib/pricing.ts), and places that violate CLAUDE.md golden rules. Be specific with file:line.' },
  { key: 'ux-polish', prompt: 'DIMENSION: Product UX & polish. Read the page components across marketing/auth/browse/booking/session/account/provider/admin and the design brief (Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md). Assess: empty/loading/error-state coverage, responsive/mobile behavior (the app is desktop-first 85%-width capped 1500px — does it degrade gracefully?), microcopy consistency vs the brief\'s voice, onboarding friction, discoverability of key actions (talk now, favorite, rebook, report), and any rough edges a real user would hit. Concrete, not vague.' },
]

phase('Assess')
const assessed = await parallel(DIMS.map((d) => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${d.prompt}`, { label: `assess:${d.key}`, phase: 'Assess', agentType: 'Explore', schema: SCHEMA })
    .then((r) => ({ dim: d.key, findings: (r?.findings ?? []) }))
))

const all = assessed.filter(Boolean).flatMap((a) => a.findings.map((f) => ({ ...f, dim: a.dim })))
log(`Assessment gathered ${all.length} findings across ${assessed.filter(Boolean).length} dimensions.`)

phase('Synthesize')
const ROADMAP_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['topRisks', 'quickWins', 'roadmap', 'deferred'],
  properties: {
    topRisks: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'highest-severity correctness/security items to fix first' },
    quickWins: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'high-value low-effort (S) items' },
    roadmap: { type: 'array', items: {
      type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['rank', 'theme', 'severity', 'effort', 'items', 'rationale'],
      properties: {
        rank: { type: 'number' },
        theme: { type: 'string' },
        severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['high', 'medium', 'low'] },
        effort: { type: 'string', enum: ['S', 'M', 'L', 'XL'] },
        items: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        rationale: { type: 'string' },
      },
    } },
    deferred: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'intentionally-out-of-scope items (documented), for completeness' },
  },
}
const synthesis = await agent(
  `You are the synthesis lead. Below are raw assessment findings (JSON) from 7 dimensions of the ` +
  `Heard codebase. Dedupe overlapping items, drop anything that is clearly a documented intentional ` +
  `deferral (list those under "deferred"), and produce a PRIORITIZED roadmap. Rank themes by ` +
  `(severity × value ÷ effort). Surface the top correctness/security risks first, then quick wins, ` +
  `then the ranked roadmap of larger themes. Be concrete and honest — this product's users are blind, ` +
  `so accessibility and safety regressions matter most.\n\nFINDINGS JSON:\n${JSON.stringify(all)}`,
  { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize', schema: ROADMAP_SCHEMA }
)

return { dimensionCount: assessed.filter(Boolean).length, findingCount: all.length, ...synthesis, rawByDim: assessed.filter(Boolean).map((a) => ({ dim: a.dim, count: a.findings.length })) }

  why: The product's entire premise is dignity and usability for blind/low-vision users; a11y defects are the highest-value-to-fix class. Bundle the smaller a11y polish (focus, timer, toggle state, nav landmark) into the same pass since they touch the same files and reviewer context.

   - Dialog initial focus management (autoFocus first focusable after showModal) — components/ui/Dialog.tsx
   - Session timer screen-reader announcement: milestone announcements via Toast, not per-second aria-live — CallStage.tsx
   - Reinforce mute/captions toggle state with non-color cues (text/border) for color-blind users — CallStage.tsx:99-121
   - Wrap header navigation in a <nav> landmark — components/shared/AppHeader.tsx

#2 [high/S] Suspension/safety enforcement and money-copy correctness
  why: Small, surgical fixes to correctness/safety invariants the spec explicitly mandates (commission never a literal; suspension = full lockdown). Very low effort, directly protects money math and bad-actor containment for a vulnerable user base.
   - Add is_suspended guards to declineBooking and setAvailability — app/(provider)/provider/actions.ts:80-109
   - Interpolate commission copy from getCommissionRate() instead of literal 95%/5% — messages/en.json:114 + onboarding step 3
   - Extract magic +15 buffer to a named CALL_SESSION_BUFFER_MINUTES constant — app/(customer)/session/actions.ts:53
   - Add a friendly 'listener unavailable' path when a provider is suspended/offline mid-booking — book/[providerId]/page.tsx

#3 [high/L] Test coverage for critical paths (server actions, RLS, accounting, suspension)
  why: Highest-leverage durable risk reduction: these guard the auth/ownership and money invariants that this two-sided marketplace depends on. RLS untested means a misconfigured policy ships silently; action-level tests catch payment and authorization bugs the component-mocked tests cannot. Large effort but blocks the most expensive class of production incident.
   - RLS enforcement test suite against a real/isolated Supabase: per-table cross-tenant read/write denial (bookings, sessions, payouts, reviews, payments, reports, providers)
   - Server-action integration tests: createBooking (suspended parties), endSession accounting (overage→commission→earnings→capture), cancelBooking time windows, setUserSuspended status cascades, completeOnboarding field combos
   - Full end-session accounting integration test (startSession→elapsed→endSession→capture amount→session row→booking status)
   - Suspension enforcement tests (customer can't book suspended provider; provider can't toggle availability/join)
   - Pricing edge cases: rounding boundaries, fractional commission, very long sessions, invalid blockMinutes
   - Earnings aggregation edge cases (week/month boundaries, null dates, empty sessions w/ pending payouts) — lib/earnings.ts

#4 [high/L] Production readiness for real-money operation
  why: These don't block the mock-mode MVP but become hard launch gates the moment real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr go live (per CLAUDE.md out-of-scope flips). CI gaps actively let regressions merge today, so the CI + observability + env-validation items are worth pulling forward even before real integrations; webhooks/rate-limiting can land with the integration milestone.
   - Complete CI: add `npm run build` + Playwright e2e job (spin up local Supabase, db reset) with DB isolation/global setup — .github/workflows/ci.yml, playwright.config.ts
   - Error monitoring + structured logging (Sentry/pino) for actions, route handlers, and payment/session state changes — currently only a client console.error in app/error.tsx
   - Startup env-var validation via Zod (lib/env.ts): required keys per INTEGRATIONS_MODE, valid PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE, fail loud
   - Webhook handlers (app/api/webhooks/payments, /calls) with signature verification + idempotency — required before flipping to real integrations
   - Health-check endpoint + post-deploy verification; document migration rollback/reversibility strategy
   - Rate limiting on booking/session-creation server actions

#5 [medium/M] UX polish for vulnerable / low-vision users
  why: Reduces friction and anxiety for the lonely/vulnerable target audience and prevents costly mistakes (accidental session-end charges, lost crisis access). Medium severity because flows function today, but several items (confirm-before-end, loading announcements, sticky crisis link) double as accessibility improvements, raising their value.
   - Confirm-before-end on in-progress sessions + beforeunload warning — CallStage.tsx
   - Browse: empty-state guidance + 'Clear filters', loading feedback on filter apply (useTransition + announced 'Loading listeners'), favorited-state visual+label on cards
   - VoicePlayer loading/error states ('Loading audio…', 'Audio unavailable; transcript below')
   - Sticky/persistent crisis + report access (SafetyBanner) reachable without scrolling
   - Account page density: collapsible/tabbed sections to reduce magnifier cognitive load
   - Pre-call mic-check affordance + 'what to expect' + prominent cancel — SessionFlow.tsx
   - Clarify tip 'Skip' prominence and post-call billing explanation; reschedule UI exposure on UpcomingBookings
   - Provider 'Profile health': 'Action required' + per-item 'Fix this' links for rejected/suspended

#6 [low/M] Code quality and maintainability debt
  why: Lowers future-change cost and reduces a class of latent bugs (type-cast escapes, inconsistent statuses, conflated error messages). Low severity and partly overlapping with higher-ranked work — schedule opportunistically, and do LinkButton/escapeFilterTerm/RLS-doc items alongside the a11y and security passes they reinforce.
   - LinkButton component (also resolves the rank-1 a11y fix — do once)
   - Replace 'as unknown as PublicProvider[]' double casts with type guards / Supabase generics — lib/db/queries.ts
   - Centralize fieldErrorsFrom() Zod-error mapping into lib/validation/utils.ts
   - Share StatusConfig<T> map + table column shapes across customer/provider/admin dashboards
   - Differentiate VoiceIntroRecorder error messages (permission vs unsupported vs upload)
   - Document RLS assumptions atop lib/db/queries.ts; add escapeFilterTerm helper + golden rule for .or()/.filter()
   - Prune unused i18n 'page.*' keys; clarify Dialog catch-block comments and PUBLIC_PROVIDER_COLUMNS comment

=== DEFERRED (intentional) ===
  - Messaging between customers and listeners — DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §1 'Later', SPEC.md §12 out of scope. No schema/route/component; correctly deferred.
  - Subscriptions / recurring billing — SPEC.md §12 and CLAUDE.md explicitly out of scope. Pricing is per-block only; schema/adapters kept ready.
  - Performance analytics (profile views, voice-intro plays, conversion) — DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §1 'Later'. No tracking tables; documented deferral.
  - Spending summary aggregate on customer dashboard — DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §2 'Later'. Individual payments/receipts present; aggregate view deferred.
  - Notification dispatch + preferences UI — table exists (M10) but unused; settings shows a mock 'On' badge. Deferred per DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §1/§2. Note: add the missing INSERT policy on the notifications table when this is built (currently SELECT/UPDATE only, blocking inserts).
  - Language/locale switching UI — profiles.locale column + i18n.ts ready, English-only per SPEC.md §1. Read-only display intentional; selector deferred.
  - Editable admin config (commission rate in DB) — DASHBOARDS_REQUIREMENTS.md §3 'Later'; currently read from PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE env, displayed read-only. Optional app_config table is a documented fast-follow.
  - PDF receipts — current plain-text receipt is functional and screen-reader friendly; PDF is a nice-to-have, keep text fallback. Documented as intentional.
  - Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr integration implementations — real.ts stubs throw NotImplemented by design; out of scope until the integration milestone (linked design docs recommended at that time).
  - GDPR/CCPA compliance docs, data-residency, audit-log table — legal/product decision, not a code blocker for mock-mode MVP.
  - 200%-zoom/reflow and ultra-small-screen (<320px) automated tests — test-coverage gaps (design is responsive); worth adding but not a shipping blocker. Note: app is intentionally desktop-first per project memory.
  - Favorites table — already fully implemented and integrated (addFavorite/removeFavorite + FavoriteListeners). No action needed; listed only to confirm it is NOT an open gap.

content.text:
All four spot-checks confirm the assessment is accurate, including two genuine bugs:

- ✅ **Suspended-provider hole is real** — `declineBooking` (actions.ts:84) and `setAvailability` (actions.ts:100) only call `requireRole("provider")`; unlike `createBooking`/`startSession`, neither checks `is_suspended`. A suspended listener can keep flipping "available now" and resurface in browse.
- ✅ **Hardcoded commission copy is real** — `step3Help` literally says *"You keep 95% — Heard's fee is 5%"* (en.json:114), violating golden rule 3. If `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE` changes, onboarding contradicts the live admin number.
- ✅ **CI gap is real** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only typecheck/lint/test; no `build`, no Playwright e2e.
- ✅ **Notifications table** has SELECT+UPDATE policies but **no INSERT policy** (would block the feature when built).

Here's the grounded "what else," ranked by value ÷ effort:

## 🔴 Confirmed bugs to fix first (small, surgical)
1. **Suspension lockdown gap** — add the `is_suspended` guard to `declineBooking` + `setAvailability` (copy the existing `createBooking` pattern). ~4 lines, closes a bad-actor containment hole for a vulnerable user base.
2. **Commission literal → live rate** — interpolate take-home/fee from `getCommissionRate()` in the onboarding step-3 copy instead of "95% / 5%".
3. **CI: add `npm run build`** (and ideally a Playwright e2e job with a throwaway Supabase) so broken builds / `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` regressions can't merge.

## 🟠 Highest-leverage theme: Accessibility in interactive controls (the product's whole point)
- **The `<Link><Button>` nested-interactive pattern** (`<a><button>`, 20+ sites) — a hard WCAG 2.5.1 fail where AT announces "link" but the focused role is "button". Fix once with a `LinkButton` primitive (Button that accepts `href`/`as`). This is the item I flagged last turn — the audit independently ranked it #1.
- Dialog initial-focus, the live-call timer announcing every second (should announce milestones via Toast instead), non-color cues on mute/captions toggles, and a `<nav>` landmark on the header — all bundle into the same pass.

## 🟡 Durable risk reduction (larger)
- **Test coverage for the invariants that matter**: there are **zero RLS-enforcement tests and zero server-action tests**. Nothing verifies cross-tenant denial (a customer reading another's bookings/earnings) or the money path (`endSession` accounting → capture, `cancelBooking` time windows, `setUserSuspended` cascades). This is the most expensive class of incident to ship blind.
- **Production readiness** (only matters at real-money flip, but CI/env-validation/observability worth pulling forward): startup env validation via Zod, structured error monitoring, webhook handlers with signature + idempotency, rate limiting on booking/session actions.

## 🟢 UX polish for vulnerable users
Confirm-before-end on a live call (a stray click shouldn't cut off a caller mid-conversation), Browse empty-state + "Clear filters", VoicePlayer loading/error states, and a sticky crisis/report link (currently only reachable by scrolling to the footer).

## ⚪️ Correctly deferred (no action)
Messaging, subscriptions, performance analytics, spending summary, notification dispatch, language switcher, editable commission, PDF receipts, real integrations — all documented as out-of-scope in SPEC §12 / the dashboards "Later" columns, with schema/adapters kept ready.

---

The natural next PR is the **three confirmed bugs** (rank-2 quick wins — small, high-value, safety/money correctness) — I can knock those out and ship them now. After that, the **`LinkButton` accessibility refactor** is the highest-value larger piece. Want me to do the quick-win fixes now, start the `LinkButton` work, or open GitHub issues for the full roadmap so it's tracked?

## Deploying

The app deploys as **Next.js on Vercel** + **Supabase Cloud** (Postgres/Auth/Storage),
running in `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock` until the real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr adapters are wired.

1. **Create a Supabase project** at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) and note its project ref + API keys (Settings → API).
2. **Push the schema** from this repo:
   ```bash
   supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
   supabase db push            # applies everything in supabase/migrations/
   ```
   `supabase/seed.sql` is sample/demo data — run it only on a staging/demo project, never on real production data.
3. **Auth URLs:** in Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration, set the Site URL and add your Vercel domain (and `http://localhost:3000`) to the redirect allow-list.
4. **Import the repo into Vercel** and set the environment variables (from [`.env.example`](.env.example)):
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — from Supabase API settings
   - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — server-only secret; **never** expose to the client
   - `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`, `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard`
5. **Build & deploy** — Vercel auto-detects Next.js (`next build`). CI already gates `typecheck · lint · test · build` on every PR.

When real integrations land, set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`, fill the Stripe/Zoom/Checkr keys (commented in `.env.example`), and implement the `lib/integrations/*/real.ts` stubs. Webhook handlers, structured error monitoring, and rate limiting are recommended at that point (tracked as fast-follows).

## Project shape

## Project shape
toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Heard

A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with — and be listened to by —
professional companion listeners, all of whom are legally blind or visually
impaired. **Companionship and conversation, not therapy.** Accessibility is the
product, not a layer.

See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for the full build spec, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
the conventions every change follows, and [`BUILD_PLAN.md`](BUILD_PLAN.md) for
the milestones.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth +
Storage) · Tailwind v4 · Zod · Vitest + Testing Library + `jest-axe` ·
Playwright. External services (payments, calls, background checks) are reached
only through adapters and run in **mock** mode by default.

## Prerequisites

- Node 20+ and npm.
- A local container runtime + the Supabase CLI. On macOS without Docker Desktop,
  a headless setup works:

  ```sh
  brew install supabase/tap/supabase colima docker
  colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
  ```

  Colima exposes its Docker socket at `~/.colima/default/docker.sock`. If the
  Supabase/Docker CLIs can't find it, export:

  ```sh
  export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"
  ```

## Setup

```sh
npm install
supabase start                 # applies migrations in supabase/migrations/
supabase db reset              # apply migrations + seed (6 providers, admin, customer)
supabase status -o env         # copy the keys below into .env.local
```

Create `.env.local` (see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) using the values from
`supabase status`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<ANON_KEY>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<SERVICE_ROLE_KEY>
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
```

Then:

```sh
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

### Try it — seeded accounts

All seeded accounts use the password **`password123`**:

| Role     | Email                  | What you can do                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Customer | `customer@heard.test`  | Browse, book, run a mock call, rate + tip        |
| Listener | `maya@heard.test`      | Dashboard, availability, sessions, earnings      |
| Admin    | `admin@heard.test`     | Approve/reject/suspend listeners, run payouts    |

(There are 6 seeded listeners: maya, theo, ines, walter, priya, omar.)

> Local notes:
> - `supabase/config.toml` disables the `analytics` (Vector) container — it
>   bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's virtiofs mount doesn't support.
> - `next.config.ts` sets `allowedDevOrigins` so server actions work when the dev
>   server is driven from `127.0.0.1` (Playwright).

## Scripts

```sh
npm run dev          # local dev
npm run build        # production build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
npm run test         # vitest (unit + component, incl. axe a11y checks)
npm run test:e2e     # playwright (needs local Supabase + dev server)
npm run db:reset     # supabase db reset (re-applies migrations + seed)
```

### End-to-end tests

The two Playwright happy paths (`tests/e2e/`) drive the real app, so they need a
running local Supabase with a fresh seed:

```sh
supabase db reset
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm run test:e2e
```

They cover: (a) customer browse → book → mock session → rate; (b) provider
onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.

## Database types

`lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is generated from the live schema. Regenerate
after any migration:

```sh
supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public > lib/supabase/database.types.ts
```

## Swapping a mock adapter for a real one

Every external service is behind an adapter in
`lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/`, each with
`interface.ts` · `mock.ts` · `real.ts` · `index.ts`. Feature code only ever
calls `getPayments()` / `getCalls()` / `getBackgroundCheck()` from `index.ts` —
it never imports `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and the external SDKs are only
imported inside `real.ts`.

To go live with one (e.g. payments):

1. Implement the methods in `lib/integrations/payments/real.ts` against the SDK
   (the `// TODO` stubs mark each one). Keep the same `interface.ts` contract.
2. Add the provider's keys to your environment (see the commented block in
   [`.env.example`](.env.example)).
3. Set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`. `index.ts` then returns the real adapter;
   nothing else in the app changes.

Mappings: **payments → Stripe Connect** (Express accounts host funds + payouts),
**calls → Zoom Meeting SDK** (platform-owned host pool + S2S OAuth + webhook
metering), **background-check → Checkr**. The build already compiles in
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`; calling a method just reaches its `// TODO` stub until
implemented.

## Project shape

```
app/                 route groups: (marketing) (auth) (customer) (provider) (admin)
components/          ui/ (design-system primitives) + customer/ provider/ admin/ session/ shared/
lib/                 integrations/  supabase/  db/queries.ts  validation/schemas.ts  pricing.ts  auth.ts
messages/en.json     all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
supabase/            migrations/  seed.sql  config.toml
tests/               unit/  component/  e2e/
```

## Status

**Build complete (M0–M9).** All routes implemented; both E2E happy paths pass;
integrations run in mock mode end-to-end with a seeded set of 6 providers, and
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to the clearly-marked `// TODO` stubs. All
money flows through `lib/pricing.ts` (integer cents, commission from config);
RLS is enforced on every table; accessibility is axe-checked across components.
Fast-follows (real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, a moderation UI, native mobile,
subscriptions) are intentionally out of scope — the schema and adapters are
ready for them.

# Heard

A two-sided marketplace where people pay to talk with — and be listened to by —
professional companion listeners, all of whom are legally blind or visually
impaired. **Companionship and conversation, not therapy.** Accessibility is the
product, not a layer.

See [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) for the full build spec, [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
the conventions every change follows, and [`BUILD_PLAN.md`](BUILD_PLAN.md) for
the milestones.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth +
Storage) · Tailwind v4 · Zod · Vitest + Testing Library + `jest-axe` ·
Playwright. External services (payments, calls, background checks) are reached
only through adapters and run in **mock** mode by default.

## Prerequisites

- Node 20+ and npm.
- A local container runtime + the Supabase CLI. On macOS without Docker Desktop,
  a headless setup works:

  ```sh
  brew install supabase/tap/supabase colima docker
  colima start --cpu 2 --memory 4
  ```

  Colima exposes its Docker socket at `~/.colima/default/docker.sock`. If the
  Supabase/Docker CLIs can't find it, export:

  ```sh
  export DOCKER_HOST="unix://$HOME/.colima/default/docker.sock"
  ```

## Setup

```sh
npm install
supabase start                 # applies migrations in supabase/migrations/
supabase db reset              # apply migrations + seed (6 providers, admin, customer)
supabase status -o env         # copy the keys below into .env.local
```

Create `.env.local` (see [`.env.example`](.env.example)) using the values from
`supabase status`:

```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<ANON_KEY>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<SERVICE_ROLE_KEY>
INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock
PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
```

Then:

```sh
npm run dev                    # http://localhost:3000
```

### Try it — seeded accounts

All seeded accounts use the password **`password123`**:

| Role     | Email                  | What you can do                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Customer | `customer@heard.test`  | Browse, book, run a mock call, rate + tip        |
| Listener | `maya@heard.test`      | Dashboard, availability, sessions, earnings      |
| Admin    | `admin@heard.test`     | Approve/reject/suspend listeners, run payouts    |

(There are 6 seeded listeners: maya, theo, ines, walter, priya, omar.)

> Local notes:
> - `supabase/config.toml` disables the `analytics` (Vector) container — it
>   bind-mounts the Docker socket, which Colima's virtiofs mount doesn't support.
> - `next.config.ts` sets `allowedDevOrigins` so server actions work when the dev
>   server is driven from `127.0.0.1` (Playwright).

## Scripts

```sh
npm run dev          # local dev
npm run build        # production build
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
npm run test         # vitest (unit + component, incl. axe a11y checks)
npm run test:e2e     # playwright (needs local Supabase + dev server)
npm run db:reset     # supabase db reset (re-applies migrations + seed)
```

### End-to-end tests

The two Playwright happy paths (`tests/e2e/`) drive the real app, so they need a
running local Supabase with a fresh seed:

```sh
supabase db reset
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm run test:e2e
```

They cover: (a) customer browse → book → mock session → rate; (b) provider
onboard → admin approve → appears in browse.

## Database types

`lib/supabase/database.types.ts` is generated from the live schema. Regenerate
after any migration:

```sh
supabase gen types typescript --local --schema public > lib/supabase/database.types.ts
```

## Swapping a mock adapter for a real one

Every external service is behind an adapter in
`lib/integrations/{payments,calls,background-check}/`, each with
`interface.ts` · `mock.ts` · `real.ts` · `index.ts`. Feature code only ever
calls `getPayments()` / `getCalls()` / `getBackgroundCheck()` from `index.ts` —
it never imports `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly, and the external SDKs are only
imported inside `real.ts`.

To go live with one (e.g. payments):

1. Implement the methods in `lib/integrations/payments/real.ts` against the SDK
   (the `// TODO` stubs mark each one). Keep the same `interface.ts` contract.
2. Add the provider's keys to your environment (see the commented block in
   [`.env.example`](.env.example)).
3. Set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`. `index.ts` then returns the real adapter;
   nothing else in the app changes.

Mappings: **payments → Stripe Connect** (Express accounts host funds + payouts),
**calls → Zoom Meeting SDK** (platform-owned host pool + S2S OAuth + webhook
metering), **background-check → Checkr**. The build already compiles in
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`; calling a method just reaches its `// TODO` stub until
implemented.

## Deploying

The app deploys as **Next.js on Vercel** + **Supabase Cloud** (Postgres/Auth/Storage),
running in `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock` until the real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr adapters are wired.

1. **Create a Supabase project** at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) and note its project ref + API keys (Settings → API).
2. **Push the schema** from this repo:
   ```bash
   supabase link --project-ref <your-project-ref>
   supabase db push            # applies everything in supabase/migrations/
   ```
   `supabase/seed.sql` is sample/demo data — run it only on a staging/demo project, never on real production data.
3. **Auth URLs:** in Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration, set the Site URL and add your Vercel domain (and `http://localhost:3000`) to the redirect allow-list.
4. **Import the repo into Vercel** and set the environment variables (from [`.env.example`](.env.example)):
   - `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — from Supabase API settings
   - `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — server-only secret; **never** expose to the client
   - `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock`, `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard`
5. **Build & deploy** — Vercel auto-detects Next.js (`next build`). CI already gates `typecheck · lint · test · build` on every PR.

When real integrations land, set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`, fill the Stripe/Zoom/Checkr keys (commented in `.env.example`), and implement the `lib/integrations/*/real.ts` stubs. Webhook handlers, structured error monitoring, and rate limiting are recommended at that point (tracked as fast-follows).

## Project shape

```
app/                 route groups: (marketing) (auth) (customer) (provider) (admin)
components/          ui/ (design-system primitives) + customer/ provider/ admin/ session/ shared/
lib/                 integrations/  supabase/  db/queries.ts  validation/schemas.ts  pricing.ts  auth.ts
messages/en.json     all user-facing copy (i18n-ready)
supabase/            migrations/  seed.sql  config.toml
tests/               unit/  component/  e2e/
```

## Status

**Build complete (M0–M9).** All routes implemented; both E2E happy paths pass;
integrations run in mock mode end-to-end with a seeded set of 6 providers, and
`INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real` compiles to the clearly-marked `// TODO` stubs. All
money flows through `lib/pricing.ts` (integer cents, commission from config);
RLS is enforced on every table; accessibility is axe-checked across components.
Fast-follows (real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr, a moderation UI, native mobile,
subscriptions) are intentionally out of scope — the schema and adapters are
ready for them.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Production image for the Heard Next.js app (standalone output).
# Built and run via docker-compose.yml on the VPS. See DEPLOY.md.

# ---- deps: install all deps (cached on package*.json) ----------------------
FROM node:22-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

# ---- builder: produce .next/standalone -------------------------------------
FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
# NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined into the client bundle at BUILD time, so they
# must be present here (passed as build args from docker-compose). Server-only
# secrets (service-role key, commission rate) are injected at RUN time instead.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
RUN npm run build

# ---- runner: minimal runtime ----------------------------------------------
FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=3000 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && adduser -S nextjs -u 1001
# Standalone server + the static assets it serves.
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

input.content:
# Heard — app + reverse proxy for a self-hosted VPS deploy.
# The self-hosted Supabase stack runs SEPARATELY (official supabase/docker
# compose); this stack runs the Next.js app and a Caddy proxy that terminates
# TLS for both the app domain and the Supabase API subdomain. See DEPLOY.md.
#
#   cp .env.production.example .env.production   # then fill it in
#   docker compose up -d --build

services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      args:
        # NEXT_PUBLIC_* are baked into the client bundle at build time.
        NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}
        NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY}
        NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME:-Heard}
    image: heard-app:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Server-only secrets + config, injected at runtime (never in the image).
    env_file: .env.production
    expose:
      - "3000"
    networks:
      - web

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: ${APP_DOMAIN}
      SUPABASE_API_DOMAIN: ${SUPABASE_API_DOMAIN}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    # Lets Caddy reach the self-hosted Supabase Kong gateway, which the official
    # Supabase compose should bind to 127.0.0.1:8000 on the host (see DEPLOY.md).
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    networks:
      - web

networks:
  web:

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=

# ---- App config ------------------------------------------------------------
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME=Heard
# mock = in-app stubs (no Stripe/Zoom/Checkr). Keep mock until real adapters land.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Apply Heard's SQL migrations (in filename order) to a self-hosted Supabase
# Postgres. Idempotent only on a fresh DB — run once after the DB is up.
#
# Usage:
#   DB_URL="postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@localhost:5432/postgres" \
#     ./scripts/apply-migrations.sh
#
# Needs the `psql` client (apt install postgresql-client). Alternatively run the
# SQL inside the Supabase db container — see DEPLOY.md.
set -euo pipefail

DB_URL="${DB_URL:-}"
if [[ -z "$DB_URL" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: set DB_URL, e.g." >&2
  echo "  DB_URL='postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@localhost:5432/postgres' $0" >&2
  exit 1
fi

MIGRATIONS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/supabase/migrations"
shopt -s nullglob
files=("$MIGRATIONS_DIR"/*.sql)
if [[ ${#files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "No migrations found in $MIGRATIONS_DIR" >&2
  exit 1
fi

for f in "${files[@]}"; do
  echo ">> applying $(basename "$f")"
  psql "$DB_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f "$f"
done

echo "✓ Applied ${#files[@]} migration(s)."
echo "NOTE: supabase/seed.sql is demo data (password123 accounts) — do NOT run it in production."

# Deploying Heard on a VPS (Contabo · Docker Compose · self-hosted Supabase)

Everything runs on one box in mock-integrations mode:

```
                     Internet
                        │  :80 / :443
                 ┌──────▼──────┐
                 │    Caddy    │  automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt)
                 └──┬───────┬──┘
       heard.tld    │       │   api.heard.tld
            ┌────────▼─┐   ┌─▼─────────────────────────┐
            │ Next app │   │ Supabase Kong (127.0.0.1) │
            │  :3000   │   │  GoTrue · PostgREST ·      │
            └──────────┘   │  Storage · Postgres        │
                           └────────────────────────────┘
   docker compose (this repo)        official supabase/docker compose
```

The app talks to Supabase over its **public** API URL (`https://api.heard.tld`), because the browser auth client needs it too. Caddy is the only thing exposed publicly; Supabase's gateway is bound to `127.0.0.1` and reached through Caddy.

---

## 0. Prerequisites

- A Contabo VPS (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04), root or sudo access. 2 vCPU / 4 GB+ recommended (Supabase's ~10 containers + the app).
- A domain with **two A records** pointing at the VPS IP:
  - `heard.tld` → the app
  - `api.heard.tld` → the Supabase API
- `psql` client for migrations: `sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-client`.

## 1. Provision the VPS

```bash
# as root
adduser deploy && usermod -aG sudo deploy
# firewall: only SSH + HTTP(S)
ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80 && ufw allow 443 && ufw enable
# Docker Engine + compose plugin
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
usermod -aG docker deploy
```

Log back in as `deploy`. Do **not** open ports 8000 (Kong) or 5432 (Postgres) to the internet.

## 2. Self-host Supabase

Use the official self-hosting compose (kept current upstream — don't vendor it):

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/supabase/supabase
cd supabase/docker
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `supabase/docker/.env`:

- Set strong secrets: `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `JWT_SECRET` (≥32 chars), and the matching `ANON_KEY` / `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` JWTs (generate with the helper at <https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker#generate-api-keys>), plus `DASHBOARD_USERNAME` / `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`.
- Point auth at your app domain:
  ```
  SITE_URL=https://heard.tld
  ADDITIONAL_REDIRECT_URLS=https://heard.tld
  API_EXTERNAL_URL=https://api.heard.tld
  SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL=https://api.heard.tld
  ```
- **Bind Kong to localhost** so only Caddy can reach it. In `supabase/docker/docker-compose.yml`, change the `kong` service ports to:
  ```yaml
  ports:
    - "127.0.0.1:8000:8000"
  ```

Start it:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Keep the printed `ANON_KEY` and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — you'll paste them into the app config next.

## 3. Configure the Heard app

```bash
cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/heard && cd heard
cp .env.production.example .env.production
```

Fill `.env.production`:

- `APP_DOMAIN=heard.tld`, `SUPABASE_API_DOMAIN=api.heard.tld`, `ACME_EMAIL=you@tld`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://api.heard.tld`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=` ← the `ANON_KEY` from step 2
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=` ← the `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` from step 2
- Leave `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=mock` and `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE=0.05`.

## 4. Apply the database schema

This creates every table, all RLS policies/triggers, and the `voice-intros` Storage bucket:

```bash
DB_URL="postgresql://postgres:YOUR_POSTGRES_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/postgres" \
  ./scripts/apply-migrations.sh
```

(No `psql`? Run it through the Supabase db container instead:
`for f in supabase/migrations/*.sql; do docker compose -f ~/supabase/docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T db psql -U postgres -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < "$f"; done`.)

> **Do not run `supabase/seed.sql` in production** — it's demo data with `password123` accounts and the "1,000 calls / 200 listeners" figures are static landing-page copy, not seeded rows.

## 5. Launch the app + Caddy

```bash
docker compose --env-file .env.production up -d --build
```

Caddy provisions Let's Encrypt certs automatically once both A records resolve to the VPS. Check:

```bash
docker compose ps
curl -I https://heard.tld          # → 200/redirect from the app
curl -I https://api.heard.tld/auth/v1/health   # → Supabase reachable
```

## 6. Create the first admin

Sign up through the app (any role), then promote that account directly in Postgres (bypasses the role-freeze trigger via a superuser connection):

```bash
psql "postgresql://postgres:YOUR_POSTGRES_PASSWORD@localhost:5432/postgres" \
  -c "update public.profiles set role='admin' where email='you@tld';"
```

Sign out/in; you'll land on `/admin`.

## 7. Updates & maintenance

```bash
git pull
docker compose --env-file .env.production up -d --build   # rebuild + restart app
# new migrations? re-run step 4 (only the new files apply cleanly on top).
```

- **Backups:** `pg_dump` the Supabase Postgres on a cron (`docker compose -f ~/supabase/docker/docker-compose.yml exec -T db pg_dump -U postgres postgres | gzip > backup-$(date +%F).sql.gz`) and snapshot the Storage volume.
- **Logs:** `docker compose logs -f app` / `caddy`.
- **Going live with real payments/calls:** set `INTEGRATIONS_MODE=real`, fill the Stripe/Zoom/Checkr keys in `.env.production`, implement `lib/integrations/*/real.ts`, and add webhook + rate-limiting handling before taking real money (tracked as fast-follows).
